⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month.
  • If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines!
  • It has been revealed that you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month. The major day is Nov. 27, but the sales have already started.

If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines! (So to speak.).

It has been revealed that you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy. Focus on the categories likely to offer the biggest savings. Here’s what to buy, and what can wait.

If you’ve got top-priority toys on your list, buy them at a discount if you can find them, states Kristin McGrath, senior editor at The Krazy Coupon Lady, “just in case they don’t go down in price later.”.

Non-electronic toys are a good bet, says Julie Ramhold, consumer analyst with DealNews.com, because they’re less affected by tariffs on electronic components. That includes Legos, dolls and playsets.

NeeDoh squishies are a hot stocking stuffer this year and may be in short supply. At authorized retailers like Target, they should be relatively affordable, but try to avoid unauthorized resellers who may crank up the price, Ramhold says.

While you may see mattress stores offering a few doorbusters on Black Friday, don’t feel pressured to jump on a deal.

“Mattresses tend to see some of their strongest discounts around major sales events like Labor Day and Presidents Day,” says Ashley Feinstein Gerstley, shopping and savings strategist with Rakuten. “So if you’re not in a rush, it may be worth waiting for one of those windows.”.

Similarly, bedding and towels are often on deep discount during January white sales, Feinstein Gerstley notes.

Recent findings suggest that got some counter space and an itch for a newly introduced food processor? Black Friday sales are a great time to price surf for countertop appliances, including blenders, juicers and air fryers.

Industry observers note that “Those things we see sometimes half off or more,” McGrath says. “And they’re all on sale at the same time, so any one you’re looking for is likely to have a discount.”.

Holiday decor is only a must-buy during Black Friday sales if you need it for this holiday season.

While you’ll still see sales on holiday items like artificial trees, drinkware and garlands, “if you can wait until after Christmas, that’s when discounts should reach up to 80% or more at stores like Target, Walmart and department stores like JCPenney and Macy’s,” Ramhold says.

Electronics are typically a slam-dunk buy at this time of year. “Every store is competing for your business, so televisions, headphones, tablets, laptops — they’re all going to be on sale at the same time,” McGrath states.

Recent findings suggest that gaming consoles, in particular, see some of the better discounts. And they often come bundled with a gift card, gaming accessories or video games. “Consoles are common gifts,” McGrath says. “The stores know that, so they’re offering competitive deals.”.

That noted, the traditional deep discounts you usually see on electronics for Black Friday may be a little lackluster this year due to high prices on parts, Ramhold states.

In a recent development, for best results, research the exact specs of the product you want and put it in your cart ahead of time, claims consumer savings expert Andrea Woroch. That way, if a similar (but not identical) product goes on sale, you won’t accidentally buy the wrong thing.

You’ll usually find deeper discounts on items that are associated with fitness resolutions after Fresh Year’s Day.

“Big-box retailers like Target and department stores like Macy’s will offer up to 40% off or more on both fitness equipment and activewear during early January sales,” Ramhold says.

According to recent reports, many fashion retailers offer Black Friday sales, McGrath states. So if there’s an item you stock in multiple colors or a work staple you need to replace, keep an eye on your favorite sites for the markdowns.

Sources indicate that shoes, too, are a category to eyeball, including seasonal buys and everyday options like running shoes, Ramhold says. “Some retailers may offer a BOGO promotion of some kind, but it’ll likely just be a ‘buy one, get one for 50% off,’” she says.

Industry observers note that just shop early for your size and color before inventory runs low, McGrath says. “You don’t want to miss out if there's a great deal.”.

According to recent reports, one caveat: Winter apparel will usually see bigger discounts toward the end of the year, Woroch claims. So wait on your boot and coat purchases if you can.

Black Friday also offers the chance to snag deals on things you can use throughout the year:.

Photo gifts: Whether you’re ordering holiday cards or putting together a photo book for your in-laws (or yourself), you can usually find sales from vendors like Snapfish and Shutterfly, among others.

Fitness classes: Try your local gym, yoga or Pilates studio for discounts on class packs. “I’ll buy a 20-class package, and it’s always a great deal,” Woroch states.

Spa services: Check local businesses for deals on massages, manicures and other self-care treatments.

Streaming subscriptions: If you’re a fresh customer (or canceled at least a month ago), some streaming platforms offer deep Black Friday discounts.

Black Friday deals are as much about strategy as savings, so make sure you’re maximizing your spending with these tips:.

Industry observers note that let AI help. Tools like ChatGPT and Gemini can do a lot of the legwork for you. Write out a product name and try prompts like “Find the lowest price for X product by comparing every retail site that it’s sold on and including coupons and cash back offers,” Woroch notes. (Just note that AI searches can be limited and may not find every deal available.).

Industry observers note that check the price, not just the percentage: “Sometimes the base price is inflated or it was listed initially for a higher price,” Feinstein Gerstley says. “Another retailer might have the same item for less, even if their discount doesn't look as impressive.”.

Use a browser extension or cash-back app. As long as you’re spending money, recapture some of it with a browser extension or cash-back app that sends a percentage of your purchase back to you.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that during the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella declared several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the tech giant.
  • Also: Microsoft states its latest AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.
  • Industry observers note that MAI said it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that during the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella declared several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the tech giant. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft states its latest AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.

Industry observers note that MAI said it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

“You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Company to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, noted during the keynote.

The approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft mentioned it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman mentioned during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

Industry observers note that the dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the company has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

Western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026.

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman noted of the new coding model the manufacturer revealed at Ignite.

According to recent reports, the company also released its upcoming image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

#16536. Tech Report: Polaroid’s Portable Printer Got Me Right Back Into Journaling

Tech Report: Polaroid’s Portable Printer Got Me Right Back Into Journaling

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (891 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that I loved journaling as a child.
  • I made multiple attempts to return to journaling throughout the years, with varying success.
  • Recently, however, I found a way for me to actually stick to the habit: a $110 Polaroid Hi-Print pocket printer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I loved journaling as a child. It helped me survive hormonal changes, the usual teen dramas, plus a hefty dose of existential angst. Then college called, and I moved to a different country, leaving behind my childhood, my Nirvana cassettes (I’m old, OK?) and, sadly, my journaling habit.

I made multiple attempts to return to journaling throughout the years, with varying success. I’ve delved into bullet journals under the pretense of improving my productivity, but I gave up when it became too much effort. I’ve invested in multiple notebooks and planners, only to eventually neglect them.

Recently, however, I found a way for me to actually stick to the habit: a $110 Polaroid Hi-Print pocket printer.

It all began when I discovered the wondrous world of journaling TikTok. In short-form videos, creators would show off beautiful journal pages decorated with colored markers, stickers, washi tape and, yes, photos — specifically photos from portable printers because the prints are small enough to fit within the confines of a typical journal or planner. I really liked the idea of decking out my journal pages with photos of my everyday life. I knew I had to get one.

After a bit of research, I decided on a couple of criteria. First, I wanted the printer to be a dye sublimation printer rather than a ZINK (Zero Ink) printer. Dye sublimation printers essentially use heat to transfer dye onto the paper, while ZINK printers use a special paper that activates under heat with no ink required (hence the name). Dye sublimation prints tend to be higher quality because it transfers the dye in layers of cyan, magenta and yellow, followed by a protective coating.

Second, I wanted the photo to be on sticky paper so that I didn’t have to mess around with glue to add these photos to my journal.

Recent findings suggest that I found quite a number of dye sublimation pocket printers on the market, but the one that caught my eye immediately was the Polaroid Hi-Print 2×3 Generation 2 pocket printer. I fell in love with it the moment I saw it. The sleek white design, the Polaroid logo and that curved rainbow accent on the edge really sealed the deal for me. Call me a sucker for style, I guess.

I purchased a Hi-Print 2×3 “starter set,” which includes the printer along with two 2×3 paper cartridges. Each cartridge has 10 photo sheets, and each sheet is made out of sticky back photo paper, which is exactly what I wanted. Both the Gen 2 and the prior Gen 1 are easy to find; the main difference is the newer one uses a USB-C charging port while the original uses the older Micro-USB port.

It has been revealed that getting started with the printer is simple enough: Download the Polaroid Hi-Print app, pair the printer with your phone and you’re ready to go. The app is fairly easy to navigate. I like that it lets you arrange your photos in collages so you’re not limited to just one photo per sheet. You can also decorate your prints with colorful frames or decorations. The printer even offers a mosaic option that lets you print out one significant image using multiple sheets.

Since it’s a dye sublimation printer, the Hi-Print prints out photos in stages. It lays down the different colors in multiple passes (yellow in the first pass, magenta in the second pass, and so forth). Because of that, printing does take a while: around 60 seconds per photo.

Sources indicate that but I don’t mind the delay, as the resulting photo quality is superb. The colors are vibrant and the overall image is nice and sharp. The contrast could be a little better, but for a little pocket printer, the quality definitely exceeded my expectations.

There are a few downsides, however. The obvious one is that photo cartridges can be pretty expensive. One pack of 20 sheets is around $17, though you can get it for $14 each if you buy the 5-pack. That’s still almost 70 cents per 2×3 print. If you use multiple prints, that can add up pretty swiftly.

Another downside is that it doesn’t have a super long battery life. It only has a 620mAh battery, which Polaroid notes will last up to 20 photo printing sessions. I only ever use this printer at home, so this isn’t a massive deal for me, but I can see this being a potential disappointment if you want to bring this printer on the road. That noted, if you do want to charge it, it doesn’t take that long. Polaroid says it takes under an hour, and that feels about right based on my experience.

I’ve had this printer for a few months now, and I’m very pleased with it. Since I use the photos primarily with my journal, I also really appreciate how thin the photo sheets are, so they don’t bulk up the pages too much. I truly enjoy printing out my little creations, cutting out my collages and then decorating my journal with them.

I might not have my childhood back nor my Nirvana cassettes, but at least I’ve finally recaptured the joys of journaling — even if it did require a bit of help from a pocket printer.

But what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is at the moment expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

In a recent development, this is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some crucial ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. It has been revealed that desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

#16532. Everything Is Falling Apart, and AI’s Fingerprints Are All Over It

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2219 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Everything Is Falling Apart, and AI’s Fingerprints Are All Over It

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2219 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I have struggled to find the time to write this story about why everything keeps breaking because everything keeps breaking.
  • But even before that, you had issues if you ran a website with PHP, or had a grocery store freezer connected to the internet, or owned crypto.
  • In a recent development, something must be behind all of this, you might think—a massive cyberattack campaign, maybe or AI agents running amok across the internet?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I have struggled to find the time to write this story about why everything keeps breaking because everything keeps breaking.

Microsoft Outlook? Broken, for a bit. Air traffic control? Had some problems. Bank with Chase? Monday was not great. But even before that, you had issues if you ran a website with PHP, or had a grocery store freezer connected to the internet, or owned crypto. I am almost certainly forgetting some.

In a recent development, something must be behind all of this, you might think—a massive cyberattack campaign, maybe or AI agents running amok across the internet? But the answer is more complicated than that. All of these issues, and the ones that will happen after I write this, are probably unconnected, at least in the concrete sense. But they exist in a world where the infrastructure of the internet and the whole human world it undergirds looks increasingly precarious.

Industry observers note that adam Meyers, senior vice president of counter adversary operations at cybersecurity organization CrowdStrike, called last month “Black October.” This month? “Blacker November.” December probably isn’t looking great.

“This is not getting better, unfortunately,” Meyers told me.

One massive reason for all of this, although not the only one, is artificial intelligence, but maybe not in the ways you expect.

Sources indicate that if it’s connected to the internet, it’s at risk. Websites, sure. But also utilities like power plants and water treatment facilities or, for some reason, grocery store freezers.

In the olden days, like six months ago, a hacker taking control would have required a fairly complicated set of skills, honed over a long career, perhaps in the employ of a government or criminal organization.

In a recent development, artificial intelligence, especially models developed and released this year, has changed things. AI has “democratized” hacking, cybersecurity experts told me. Things that used to require the capabilities and focus of a team of people with a clear goal can be done by a 20-something with an AI model and a specially designed program around it. And you don’t have to be a big or valuable target anymore to be worthy of a hacker’s attention.

Industry observers note that at the same time, AI has made it easier to find vulnerabilities. These models and agents — essentially AI models that can do things on their own — can comb through websites or code and find problems that might have escaped the notice of humans. And they can do so more cheaply, meaning they can be turned on code that might not otherwise have gotten a close look. So many vulnerabilities are being exposed that it’s been given an appropriately bleak name: the vulnpocalypse.

Even that defensive advantage is a double-edged sword. Before, it might have taken weeks before a newly discovered vulnerability could be exploited. Now it might take days, even hours. If you’re responsible for a website or any of those things connected to the internet that may or may not still be maintained by their creators, you may not be paying attention and know you should update. You may find yourself liable if a breach leads to a leak of customer data. You may not have the know-how to fix it.

Another risk introduced by AI is that the technology, trained on all the lines of code its creators could find, is really good at writing code. Software engineers know this, and companies are now maintaining smaller teams of human engineers using AI to write more and more software. That code might be OK, but it might not be, and there’s a chance no human ever looked at it to be sure.

In a recent development, when I connected with John Strand over video chat, he was in Germany for a conference, and he was smiling. That wasn’t good. “You need to understand that whenever an offensive security person smiles and gets excited,” he noted, “it’s bad.”.

As owner and CEO of Black Hills Information Security, Strand’s job is to test systems for weaknesses, to think like an attacker and poke holes in a client’s defenses. He states he’d been getting a bit bored with the work after decades of the same techniques until the cyber capabilities of AI models started to explode at the end of 2025. New AI models were great at finding weaknesses in code, and AI agents could do the boring, time-consuming part.

“You’re seeing something that can automate the kind of grinding grunt work of offensive security and bring that to a human operator much faster,” Strand said.

Things have only accelerated since the summer. AI agents are capable of more autonomy. And attackers have better tools to refine the often blunt instruments of AI models — harnesses. While an AI model can do a lot of things, a harness provides the tools and direction that allow it to do a specific thing more effectively. Think Anthropic’s Claude Code or OpenAI’s Codex, but for hacking. Perhaps the biggest, most notable harness used by hackers is Artex, a significant-enough threat that the FBI issued a warning last week.

In September and October, a hack of major South Korean banks led to the theft of personal information. Meyers claims CrowdStrike determined the attacker was likely a 26-year-old in China using Artex. After asking AI how to do the attack, the hacker succeeded, then asked the AI how to sell the stolen data on Telegram.

“Anybody out there can now be a nation-state-level hacker just by using the tool,” Meyers stated.

Despite efforts by major AI developers to limit who can access their biggest and most capable models, the hacking and exploit skills attackers need are within the means of models already in the hands of attackers. That includes open-weight models that hackers can run on their own hardware, away from the guardrails and peering eyes of AI companies and government agencies.

“The genie’s out of the bottle, and there’s no putting it back in,” said Gary Barlet, public sector chief technology officer at Illumio, a firm that specializes in ransomware and breach containment.

Recent findings suggest that AI-powered hackers, whether they’re individual vibe-hackers or government-backed cyberwarfare units intent on damaging critical infrastructure, always have an advantage. They just have to be right once, as the saying goes. Defenders have to be right every time.

The good thing is that the defenders are using the same tools as the attackers. And sometimes they have a head start. Programs like Anthropic’s Project Glasswing, OpenAI’s Daybreak and Google’s Fairwind let cybersecurity experts and high-profile targets like banks and healthcare providers have early access to the most capable models from those developers, often with fewer limits on what the models can find. The goal is to get a jump on patching and fixing the easiest and riskiest problems.

It has been revealed that it still might not be enough, and Massive Tech leaders know it. In an October appearance at the Stanford Graduate School of Business, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman mentioned he no longer thought we’d be able to “just patch all the bugs” and that the problem is one that “is still something that we have not, as organizational leaders or countries or individuals, taken seriously.”.

In a recent development, and defenders may not have much of a lead in patching bugs anyway, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella remarked this week at the Upcoming York Times Dealbook Summit. Previously, when patching a critical system, you might have a week to test it before pushing it to production. “Right now the patch needs to go instantly from being available to being patched in production because it’s being exploited in the wild,” Nadella said. “That’s going to create instability.”.

The PHP vulnerability widely reported in October — with an urgent notice from the PHP Foundation for website owners to patch — stemmed from work through Patch the Planet, part of OpenAI’s Daybreak.

Industry observers note that that’s just one high-profile recent disclosure. But there has been an avalanche of them. The National Vulnerability Database has received more than 10,000 instances of common vulnerabilities and exposures so far in November, after more than 17,000 CVEs in October. For comparison, in October 2025, that figure was less than 5,000.

“There’s effectively this substantial backlog of security concerns in the open-source world that hadn’t been discovered until AI was able to just spend tons of time analyzing it and finding these vulnerabilities,” remarked Matt Wyckhouse, CEO of Finite State, a cybersecurity firm focused on connected devices.

Recent findings suggest that it goes well beyond open-source software. The connected devices Wyckhouse focuses on include things like refrigerators and smart home gadgets — the kinds of things that probably didn’t have to be connected to the internet, but are. The source code of the firmware and software powering those products has been seen by far fewer eyes than something like PHP, an incredibly common coding language used by much of the internet. The code running these devices may not be on GitHub or floating around the internet, but an AI model might be able to reverse-engineer it and find an exploit. And suddenly an attacker can turn freezers into ovens. If you think ground beef is expensive now, imagine what would happen if a major retailer’s stock of hamburger all spoiled overnight.

“Refrigeration has to work for our society to function, as it turns out,” Wyckhouse said.

Wherever the vulnerability is found, it has to be patched. That’s where the backlog of challenges is really wreaking havoc. Companies that create or just operate software are swamped with notable, critical issues that have to be fixed now because it could only be hours before an attacker can exploit it. It’s why your computer and the software on it have to update so frequently these days.

“It’s daunting the amount of work and the amount of time it’s going to take to clean this whole thing up,” noted Ted Miracco, CEO of the mobile security firm Approov.

According to recent reports, and patching isn’t perfect. Sometimes it’s not a cyberattack that causes a system to go down but the fix to prevent it. Software updates are believed to be responsible for several of the recent high-profile outages, including Apple’s concerns on Tuesday.

Things get even hairier if the code isn’t great to begin with or presents upcoming problems of its own. And with AI writing even more of it, that’s a growing concern.

Sources indicate that in the backdrop of all of this chaos is the fact that software engineering is one of the industries most disrupted by AI. Models trained on miles of code are great at writing something that works — no matter how many holes are in it. And to CEOs eager to cut costs and boost their companies’ stock prices, the temptation is to lay off engineers and have fewer people use AI to do all that coding.

It has been revealed that substantial Tech has been laying off staff by the thousands this year. Microsoft’s October announcement that it was offering buyouts to 60,000 staff became a key talking point just weeks later when the system powering its Outlook email service went dark for a day. Might things break less often if more people were on hand to maintain them?

“I wouldn’t be surprised if companies start to backtrack on that more,” stated Ryan McCurdy, vice president of marketing at the database security firm Liquibase.

Companies might also have more junior developers writing and releasing code that would have previously gone through senior developers, with AI replacing the productivity, but not the experience, McCurdy claims.

That means the problem isn’t just the vulnerabilities in existing software, but the vulnerabilities being written into newly introduced software or patches to existing software by AI. The same technology is causing the problem, providing the solution and complicating that solution.

According to recent reports, the main thing we can do now is just… wait. Wyckhouse told me he thinks the next two years are going to be a period of growing pains as vulnerabilities are found and patched. The end result should be that everything is more stable.

“I think software is going to be an order of magnitude more secure by the end of the next year or two than it is today for this reason,” he said. “It will hurt a bit.”.

Whether you’re an ordinary phone user or a major corporation, updating your software has become more notable than ever.

It has been revealed that “You’ve got to patch. You go for a flu shot, and you go and have your preventative healthcare,” Meyers said. “You need to do the same thing when it comes to cybersecurity.”.

But consumers aren’t without power, especially when it comes to data breaches. If a firm isn’t properly maintaining its systems and protecting your privacy or security online, don’t use it. Having your data hacked and compromised has become ordinary. We get letters in the mail saying someone stole data from our bank or doctor’s office, and if we jump through the following hoops, we can get 12 months of identity protection.

We don’t have to put up with it, Barlet says. “I think we need to start having higher expectations from the companies we’re consuming from,” he said.

#16526. One Month and a Half-Million-Plus Folds Later, Our Machine Is Still Testing the iPhone Duo

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1109 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

One Month and a Half-Million-Plus Folds Later, Our Machine Is Still Testing the iPhone Duo

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1109 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple’s $1,999 iPhone Duo folding phone came out a month ago.
  • Recent findings suggest that how many times can we fold the iPhone Duo?
  • Sources indicate that I oversee hardware and software testing as director of lab operations in our lab in Louisville, Kentucky.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple’s $1,999 iPhone Duo folding phone came out a month ago. Every day since then, 24 hours a day, seven days a week, a dedicated machine inside CNET’s lab has been folding and unfolding it over and over again. For science.

Recent findings suggest that how many times can we fold the iPhone Duo? As of Friday, Nov. 20, we’re up to more than 565,000 folds and the Duo hasn’t broken yet. The hinge has shown signs of potential failure, however. Our technicians, as well as the cameras and sensors that are part of our testing rig, continue to monitor the situation and collect data.

Sources indicate that I oversee hardware and software testing as director of lab operations in our lab in Louisville, Kentucky. My team and I designed and built this proprietary machine to test foldable phones like Apple’s and its Samsung rival, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 (which we’ve also started testing). I’ve worked on the methodology and build of this testing rig for months in anticipation of Apple’s long-rumored foldable iPhone.

We even named our machine to match its purpose: Meet the Fold-a-Phone.

My team of engineers and testing experts has been watching the iPhone Duo open and close, over and over, for the past few weeks to rigorously and systematically monitor the durability of Apple’s hinge and two screens.

After all, repeatedly folding a phone with bare hands can only get you so far in understanding the complex forces at play between the magnetics that snap the screen shut and the all-critical hinge.

CNET’s Senior Technology Reporter, Abrar Al-Heeti, has done a beautiful job capturing the iPhone Duo’s pros and cons in her smart, thorough review as well as her one-month-later follow-up. Our Fold-a-Phone machine will add a deep data foundation to complement her real-world experience.

Since Apple hasn’t publicly shared claims of the iPhone Duo’s foldable lifespan, CNET’s Fold-a-Phone machine is poised to provide a wealth of valuable data about Apple’s first foldable phone and competing models in the foldable market.

And yes, you’d better believe we will use our treasure trove of in-house data to share status updates and comparisons during our ongoing testing window with the Duo.

Industry observers note that join CNET’s iPhone Duo livestream on YouTube weekdays from 1 p.m. to 5 p.m. ET, where you can follow along live and watch the Fold-a-Phone do its thing to a Duo.

The importance of this moment is hard to overstate. Apple’s appearance on the foldable smartfold frontier lags Samsung by seven years (the first Galaxy Fold went on sale in the US in September 2019). Motorola and other phone-makers have long experimented with foldable phones in every shape and size, including a trifold accordion foldable phone we first demoed in 2019.

CNET’s mobile experts, including Al-Heeti and Editor at Large Andrew Lanxon, have discussed the legitimizing effect of the iPhone Duo’s existence on the entire foldable phone landscape, which has previously felt like a new-wave fantasy rather than a mainstream riptide.

Recent findings suggest that in many ways, Apple’s newfound competition with existing foldable phones completes the portfolio. That is precisely why we’re building the Fold-a-Phone now, and why our proprietary machine, methodology and test data will enrich our collective understanding of the capabilities – and yes, limitations – of foldable phones as our true next-generation mobile device.

Most current foldable phones are rated for 200,000 to 500,000 folds. As such, we knew we needed to create a robust and adaptable machine that could accommodate book- and flip-style foldable phones of any size, dimension and hinge orientation. (Note: The Fold-a-Phone was not built for trifold phones, which present a unique element to the engineering challenge.).

Moreover, we wanted to test the phone the way people would actually use it. No one just sits around opening and closing their foldable phone at top speed all day. Rather, you open it naturally, spend a few minutes watching a video, browsing a web page, or using an app, close it, and then put it in your pocket. This may happen dozens of times per day.

Mimicking this usage on the Fold-a-Phone limits undue stress on the phone hinge and avoids generating excess heat compared to a test built for speed.

It has been revealed that we determined that a cadence of roughly 4 seconds could sidestep technical hurdles while also being reasonably fast. The foldable phone takes 1 second to open, 1 second to fully open, 1 second to close and 1 second to fully close. This cycle counts as a single completed fold. Then, the cycle repeats until either the hinge or the screen gives out.

In conceptualizing and building the Fold-a-Phone, our team has used standard, off-the-shelf components to simplify the machine’s development. The essential design consists of two armatures, distinctly designed to perform the opening and closing movements with both force and grace.

An industrial-grade stepper motor drives each armature, with the host software (running on a connected computer) deterministically adjusting the torque to complete each step of the process while also protecting the phone. If any of the several proximity sensors fail to detect the armature in the correct position, the machine stops immediately.

In a recent development, we also monitor the motors’ power usage to track how well the foldable phone opens and closes over time. We have set up cameras to capture images and video of the test from multiple angles, and we will analyze regular status updates from the computer to determine the current status of the phone and the test.

To ensure we never miss a major development, the entire rig is connected to an EcoFlow Delta 3 Plus power station to guard against electricity outages, and all the output data is saved to multiple locations.

In a recent development, to secure each phone to the machine, we use our CNET Lab Test-winning 3D printer, the Prusa Core One, to 3D-print a custom “sled” that matches each phone’s exact dimensions. We secure the phone to the sled with heavy-duty double-sided tape (yes, it works!) and then screw the sled onto the machine.

According to recent reports, there’s always room for improvement. We’re constantly looking for ways to make the machine run more smoothly and quietly without disrupting the folding rhythm.

According to recent reports, apple’s presence is already changing the game and could very well spur innovation in ways we can’t predict today. But until then, our Fold-a-Phone machine will continue to test the iPhone Duo and its competitors, and CNET’s writers will report on how well these individual hinged devices stand up to the challenge – or fold under pressure.

Recent findings suggest that the Gemini AI improvements got a real-world test during Washington state’s Railroad Fire in July 2026, when Watch Duty issued what it calls its first-ever nighttime Critical Alert. The alert stemmed from a nearly unintelligible, static-filled 911 call that the Gemini tool transcribed in under 30 seconds. That kind of assistance can help Watch Duty send alerts to affected communities more quickly and enable first responders to patch maps more accurately and make better-informed decisions.

“This is something the tool also has the capability to do if reports of flooding are communicated via radio,” mentioned Dave Merritt, co-founder and chief technology officer of Watch Duty. “Across disasters, we hear feedback every day that first responders are using Watch Duty for additional situational awareness, especially for disasters that span multiple counties.”.

Watch Duty reporters are active and retired first responders who can manually monitor up to 20 different feeds, though static and rapid-fire jargon can make them difficult to follow.

Gemini workers used more than 20,000 hours of Watch Duty radio recordings to train the AI tool to recognize firefighting terms that aren’t in the average dictionary or books that AIs are typically trained on.

Google claims the tool is not designed to replace human decision-making in life-or-death situations.

“This tool takes on the demanding work of listening, freeing Watch Duty’s volunteers to focus on what matters most: confirming fires and getting warnings to people while they can still act,” said Stephanie Chew, Google project team lead.

The project was completed at no cost thanks to a Google.org fellowship, and the resulting Watch Duty app features are free to use.

From the data collected, Gemini engineers and Watch Duty identified several measures of success.

According to recent reports, one metric was the word error rate, which fell by around 15% after the AI model was implemented. Another sign of success was a jump in Watch Duty volunteers’ satisfaction with their radio transcription tools, from around 35% to 92%.

The Gemini tool continues to analyze approximately 200 hours of radio speech traffic from 400 feeds per day. The tool was made to handle more than 10,000 radio feeds if necessary.

In a recent development, the integration could pave the way for broader use across public safety. The platform’s built-in scalability could eventually bring similar audio-clearing tools to local fire departments, 911 call centers and Coast Guard operations, where clear communication is critical under pressure.

Sure, the game may currently be console-locked to the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S, but there are still clever ways to get the game booted up when you’re on the go.

Here’s everything you need to know about the remote play features that you’ll need to take this modern Bonnie and Clyde story on the road.

So long as you have a PS5 or an Xbox with GTA 6 downloaded and ready to go, you can experience the game through smaller devices even when you’re away from home.

Both modern consoles support remote play, a feature that lets you stream your game from your home setup.

Industry observers note that if you’re looking to turn on the Xbox’s remote play feature, you need to access the Profile & System settings in the Xbox guide. From there, you need to navigate to the Devices & Connections menu and choose the Remote features option.

You’ll need to enable the remote features and put your console into sleep mode in order to pair your chosen remote play device. Remote play devices include smartphones, tablets and Windows computers.

Gamers who own a PlayStation 5 will need to follow similar steps to get remote play functioning on a mobile device. Within the PlayStation’s settings menu, navigate to the System tab and choose Remote Play. Toggle the Enable Remote Play option. From there, all of the necessary device pairing and gameplay setup will happen through the PS Remote Play app, which you can download on your handheld device.

Whether you own a PlayStation or an Xbox, you’ll want to ensure your console settings are tuned so it stays connected to the internet in rest mode. You’ll also need to enable the console to turn on via a network connection. These settings will allow you to start a remote play session anytime, even if you’ve already left your home.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re using PlayStation’s remote play feature, you don’t have to fiddle around with gaming tablets or third-party handheld devices in order to find a comfortable way to play GTA 6. Sony’s PlayStation Portal is the perfect console accessory for natural gameplay, since it retains the DualShock controller design.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 isn’t coming out on PC for a while still. That limits how many options you have when it comes to taking the game on the go with you. If (for whatever reason) you don’t have access to any remote play options, that leaves you with only the most inconvenient and unwieldy way to take the new crime simulator with you on the road.

You’ll have to lug around your PS5 or Xbox wherever you go to get in some GTA time – but hey, at least the gaming industry’s deteriorating respect for physical media means you won’t have to keep track of a disc.

The PS5 Slim is probably the easiest current-gen console to carry with you, since the digital edition weighs less than 6 pounds. But you’re giving up the best possible performance available on the PS5 Pro.

Either way, you’ll be carrying around a large, expensive piece of hardware, so this option should only be considered if you really can’t get remote play functioning for whatever reason.

According to recent reports, microsoft’s video game ecosystem is huge, with Game Pass and streaming options available for PC players. But the Xbox brand isn’t offering gamers a cheat code to play GTA 6 on their beefy rigs (or any convenient handheld devices).

GTA 6 is only available on Xbox consoles with Xbox Cloud Gaming at this time. The upside is that this option lets you play the boundary-pushing fresh game on the Xbox One, which is very close to being two console generations old.

At that point, you’re better off biting the bullet on a current-generation console and considering the available remote play options.

  • Should they withdraw money from retirement savings to have more cash on hand — but pay an early withdrawal penalty?
  • Many users responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Redditor recently shared that they were struggling to decide which financial steps to take first after a job loss.

Should they withdraw money from retirement savings to have more cash on hand — but pay an early withdrawal penalty? Or is it better to rely on the severance payout to handle expenses?

Many users responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.

For more ideas, I asked three financial experts how to manage money in the immediate aftermath of job loss.

While it’s tempting to make quick decisions about tapping into a retirement fund or selling a house, it’s better to wait on any massive moves, says Parker Wine, retirement planning advisor at the financial firm Daniel A. White & Associates in Lewes, Delaware.

Industry observers note that that’s because you need time to digest the situation and weigh the pros and cons of different options, he says. “People can get impulsive and panic, and it’s usually a bad thing to make decisions when you’re panicking,” he says.

Take your time, get second opinions and think through all of your options first, Wine suggests.

If you’re fortunate enough to receive a severance package, wait to sign it until you’ve reviewed it carefully and understand all of the details, states John Rafferty, partner and investment advisor representative at Solomon Financial in Carmel, Indiana.

For example, make sure you know about your health insurance options, such as whether you’ll receive insurance through COBRA or need to take out a latest policy in the health insurance marketplace.

Filing for unemployment and checking into any other available workplace benefits — such as help with your new job search — is also an key part of understanding what support to expect in the weeks and months ahead, Rafferty adds.

Creating a bare-bones budget stripped of “extras” like restaurant meals or travel can help the severance payment last as long as possible, Rafferty claims.

“Now that you don’t have income coming in, ask yourself, ‘How much can I spend and where?’”.

You might be able to cut back on entertainment costs, coffee runs and clothing purchases, for example.

Industry observers note that at the same time, it’s important to prioritize the essentials like mortgage payments, rent, utilities and food. Rafferty recommends calling your mortgage firm, utilities provider and any other lenders to ask if they have a hardship program for those experiencing financial challenges.

Opting in could give you more time to pay your bills or temporarily lower payments.

It’s hard to stick to a budget that eliminates all entertainment, so Rafferty suggests finding enjoyable activities that come with a low price tag. Hiking, discovering a new park and participating in free community events are all ways to enjoy downtime on a budget.

Sources indicate that “Having that release is mentally a big thing so you can stay prepared for the job search,” he says. “Otherwise, it’s easy to get down and feel negative, and we need things to help us feel positive.”.

Similarly, connecting with friends and family during this time is crucial, says Laura Adams, accredited financial counselor and financial coach in Wilmington, North Carolina.

Industry observers note that people often feel a sense of shame or embarrassment after job loss, and Adams encourages people to talk about their feelings and ask for help if needed. “Financial shame can cause us to make emotional rather than confident financial decisions,” she states.

Starting some kind of side hustle to bring in extra cash can also help bridge the gap between the job loss and your next job, Wine indicates. Substitute teaching, working at a local public golf course and driving for a rideshare service are all options he’s seen people try.

Doing something fresh also helps stave off boredom while unemployed, but he cautions that you’ll still owe taxes on any side income you bring in, so plan accordingly.

All three financial experts also emphasized that a job loss is easier to handle with an emergency savings fund you can turn to, and suggested building one up — ideally three to six months’ worth of expenses. But starting small helps, too — while employed, if possible.

The Redditor who posted the question mentioned that, like many Americans, they lacked emergency savings. This added urgency to the question of what to prioritize.

Recent findings suggest that reddit is an online forum where people share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like how to deal with job loss, so we sifted through Reddit forums to get a pulse check. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

Addas a preferred source on Google.

Although interstate commerce is not currently a reality, we will remain focused given its importance to Glass House and consumers everywhere.

Recent findings suggest that as we look outside of California, in October, we received Good Agriculture and Collection Practice, GACP certifications for our Casitas and Padaro farms from Perry Johnson Registrars Food Safety. These certifications confirm that the facilities meet the strict international and interstate safety and quality standards required for medical cannabis markets, and they represent a critical step towards supplying those markets both domestically and internationally once export is permitted. Together, the 2 farms comprise more than 0.5 million square feet of advanced greenhouse cultivation, making them amongst the largest GACP-certified facilities in the United States. Markets such as Germany, the U.K. and Switzerland require GACP-compliant operations.

It has been revealed that so these certifications expand our pathway to higher-priced medicinal markets and a meaningful larger addressable opportunity as regulatory environment continues to evolve. Now turning to our third quarter results. Third quarter revenue was $56.8 million. We produced 319,000 pounds of biomass during the quarter, a record for the company and ahead of the 246,000 pounds produced last quarter. Third quarter cost of production was $109 a pound compared to the $122 per pound reported in the second quarter of 2026 and $175 per pound in the first quarter. This marks more than a 37% cost production improvement since the first quarter.

The improvement comes from continued operational efficiency enhancement as our workforce gains experience every day, and we benefit from higher production volume across a larger footprint. We remain on track to produce approximately 1 million pounds of biomass this year and exit the year with cost of production around our current level with our long-term target of $95 per pound intact. In the second quarter of 2026, it became clear that we were growing less flower and smalls and more trim. The trim mix issue persisted into the third quarter, and our CFO estimates it cost us in excess of $10 million.

As such, our average selling price for the quarter was $151 per pound, down from $211 per pound last quarter. Let me address this decrease directly. The ASP is the combination of 3 main factors: the trim mix we sold, the yields we achieved on flower and smalls and the underlying market. The largest driver this quarter was mix. We sold a higher proportion of trim, roughly 63% of pounds sold versus the high 40s and low 50s we saw in prior periods and well above our historical best of around 45%. Flower and smalls together made up only about 37% of sales.

In a recent development, in 2024, for comparison, flower alone was closer to 37% in that quarter, and our 2027 projections target a meaningfully better mix. Part of this is timing. As we finished the second quarter with higher inventory levels than expected, we sold more inventory in the third quarter from earlier production periods that were more trim-heavy. The production mix improved during the quarter, and we expect further improvement in the fourth quarter. Because of the normal lag between harvest and sale, the sales mix in any given quarter does not fully reflect the production improvements already underway. Production quality and mix better indicate where we are heading.

Sources indicate that had we sold the mix that we actually produced during the quarter, the ASP would have been higher at today's prices at $180 a pound, about $29 higher per pound than we had achieved. As previously stated, the market is a factor as well. Flower pricing in the second quarter of '26 was actually slightly higher than the prior year. However, in the third quarter, that reversed and flower sold in the high 300s a pound this quarter versus the low 400s a year ago. California wholesale price remains compressed relative to other markets and prior years, and we do not control that.

It has been revealed that pricing is also subject to normal seasonal variation and has been softer in the back half of the year, consistent with historical patterns. What we do control is the mix and the yields, and those are the areas where we are focused. On the production side, flower and smalls per square foot ran below 2024 levels this summer. The drivers are similar to what we talked about last quarter. The genetics we had to plant coming out of last year's disruption, a large share of the workforce still early on the learning curve as we expanded capacity and the temporary off-line status of a cogeneration unit that limited CO2. Wetter weather in the first half also played a role.

Recent findings suggest that these are near-term issues, not structural ones. The key point is that we are already seeing the [ turn ]. Production mix improved during the third quarter relative to the prior quarter. Operational changes, better screening, healthier plants, improved defoliation and day-to-day execution are showing up in the numbers. We are seeing an improvement in production mix and continued progress on cost of production. These operational gains are not yet fully reflected in the financial results given the timing of sales, but they give us confidence that the trajectory is improving. It's also important to note that none of the larger capital investments we already have underway or have planned are yet reflected in these results.

In a recent development, these investments are designed to further improve yields, mix and consistency as we move through 2027 to optimize Greenhouse 5 and 6. The capital we are deploying is directed toward facility upgrades and process improvements that are intended to improve yields, mix and to support further reductions in cost of production. We recognize that the third quarter fell short on mix and average selling price. Since last year's disruption, greater scale and the use of third-party processing have made the lag between harvest and sale less predictable than it was previously, and we are working to improve that visibility. Looking to the fourth quarter, we expect the sold mix to continue improving.

Industry observers note that our current forecast has flower and smalls together approaching 45% of pounds sold, up from 37% in the third quarter, even as flower pricing follows its normal seasonal decline from the high 300s into the low 300s. The blended ASP may, therefore, remain soft in the fourth quarter, but the underlying production quality and mix appear to be heading in the right direction. As pricing typically strengthen seasonally in the first quarter, we should see the benefit of the improved mix more clearly. During the third quarter, we also made the decision to pause our hemp operations after determining that the results did not support continued investment at this time.

Recent findings suggest that this action allows us to concentrate resources on our core cannabis cultivation business where we continue to see stronger opportunities for returns. We will remain disciplined in evaluating any future hemp-related opportunities should market conditions or the economics improve. Frankly, it is this greenhouse we are most excited about when we first visited the facility in October of 2018. Recent findings suggest that in retrospect, while our excitement about Greenhouse 2 remains, turning on another massive greenhouse while we were continuing to train and expand a upcoming workforce took up a lot of the team's bandwidth and the focus. Sources indicate that and the more light we have, the better yields we have. 5 upcoming Apple Health features you should try in iOS 27.3 – if your phone qualifies

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple is kicking off a new and improved Health app next month with the release of iOS 27.3.
  • Also: Apple could build its AI health chatbot from this study – how to enroll.
  • Here are five helpful upcoming features built into the app, along with what you’ll need to access them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple is kicking off a new and improved Health app next month with the release of iOS 27.3. Instead of just recording and displaying your health-related stats, the app will tap into Apple Intelligence to analyze the data and dispense advice on how to improve your health and fitness. But that reliance on AI means you’ll need the right type of iPhone to enjoy all the benefits.

Also: Apple could build its AI health chatbot from this study – how to enroll.

Here are five helpful upcoming features built into the app, along with what you’ll need to access them.

First up, the app will offer suggestions based on data from different sources. For example, it might advise you to go for a walk at a nearby park if it detects that you’re not getting enough exercise. It may show you articles and videos about sleep if it finds that you’re not well-rested. It could also highlight possible conditions based on your lab and test results. You can easily view these recommendations from the Insights screen.

Also: Health is Tim Cook’s defining legacy – and your Apple Watch proves it.

Recent findings suggest that A new feature called Health Age compares your physical health to your actual age to show how you’re doing. The analysis draws on certain stats and lab data, such as your resting heart rate, sleep, heart rate variability (HRV), cholesterol, and A1C (average blood glucose levels), to deliver a health age, which may differ from your chronological age. The results can show you areas that may be of concern or that you need to focus on.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for.

Industry observers note that with a upcoming feature called Movement Evaluations and an iPhone and Apple Watch, the Health app can assess your flexibility, strength, balance, VO2 max (maximum oxygen absorption), and overall movement. You perform a physical routine while your iPhone “watches” you via the camera. Using built-in AI, the app will provide audio and visual feedback in real-time to tell you how you’re faring.

Apple promises that the analysis is performed on your device without recording, storing, or sharing the video.

In a recent development, the upcoming app will be able to correlate your test results with data collected by your iPhone and Apple Watch to give you a more comprehensive picture of your health. Plus, Apple and Quest Diagnostics have teamed up to offer people in the US an optional $119 bloodwork panel that covers more than 50 biomarkers to scan for different health and medical conditions.

Also: I tested the Apple Watch Series 12 heart-rate claims against my gold-standard Polar strap.

Sources indicate that normally, you need an Apple Fitness+ subscription to fire up workout videos to help you exercise. But the upcoming Health app will come with its own comprehensive set of training videos. Available from the Insights section, a series of strength exercise videos are designed to help you build your body strength. The videos cover all the key areas of your body to give you a full workout.

Some of the new features, such as the strength videos, will be available to all iPhone consumers. But the ones that rely on AI will run only on phones that support Apple Intelligence. That means you’ll need an iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max, any iPhone 16 or 17, an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, an iPhone Air, or an iPhone Duo.

Industry News: iOS 27.3 Could Bring the Redesigned Health App and a More Capable Siri AI to Your Device Soon

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1040 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple debuted the second public beta of iOS 27.3 on Thursday, Nov.
  • Apple historically releases an iOS patch in December, so I expect iOS 27.3 to land on iPhones later this year.
  • Since this is a beta, I recommend downloading it on something other than your primary device.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple debuted the second public beta of iOS 27.3 on Thursday, Nov. 19, more than two months after the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and iOS 27. The headliner here is the return of the fresh Health app: After briefly testing the redesigned Health app in an early iOS 27.2 beta, Apple has put the revamped app back in the recent beta cycle.

Apple historically releases an iOS patch in December, so I expect iOS 27.3 to land on iPhones later this year.

Since this is a beta, I recommend downloading it on something other than your primary device. This isn’t the final version of iOS 27.3, so the update might be buggy and battery life may be short, so it’s best to keep those troubles on a secondary device.

Also, since this isn’t the final version, there could be more features to land on your iPhone when Apple releases 27.3.

Here are some features developers and beta testers can try now in the second iOS 27.3 beta.

The redesigned Health app returns in the iOS 27.3 beta after Apple tested the feature in the iOS 27.2 beta process. Developers and beta testers can explore the refreshed app and see things like a fresh Longevity tab and your Health Age.

Apple wrote online that we can expect the redesigned Health app to land on devices later this year.

If developers and beta testers have an Apple Watch that is running the watchOS 27.3 beta as well as an iPhone running the iOS 27.3 beta, those folks can test out Apple’s Live Rewind and Siri Recap in Audio Intelligence.

Live Rewind allows you to pull up a text transcript of a conversation in the past 15 seconds on your Apple Watch, and Siri Recap can automatically give you a summary of meetings, conversations and other events. Live Rewind snippets are replaced by latest audio and then deleted, and Siri Recaps delete themselves after seven days if you don’t manually delete them sooner. However, you can also save both of these in the Siri app and export them to the Notes or Journal apps on your iPhone.

While both Live Rewind and Siri Recap are automatically deleted over time, I’m uncomfortable with the ability to save snippets or recaps, which raises concerns about people recording my conversations without my knowledge. Even if Audio Intelligence just summarizes what I mentioned, I still find both features creepy.

And while I recognize the utility for certain groups of people, I also think it’s better to just, y’know… talk to someone instead of asking your watch what they just mentioned.

Siri AI gets a huge upgrade in the iOS 27.3 beta. The feature can now do more actions in supported apps, like Apple Music and Messages. For example, if you go into Apple Music, you can ask Siri to create a playlist for you, and in Messages, you can ask Siri to schedule, edit or unsend messages. If you open an app and ask Siri what it can do, the digital assistant should give you some examples of its capabilities.

You can also use Siri in Safari to scan an entire webpage — even parts of the page that aren’t in your direct view — to give you helpful information. So if you are looking at a menu online, you can ask Siri to find the gluten-free or vegetarian options.

The beta also brings Siri AI to traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish and Norwegian.

In the latest iOS 27.3 beta, developers and beta testers can find video podcasts in the Apple TV app, as well as in the Podcasts app. You can find video podcasts by going into the app, tapping Home across the bottom of your screen and scrolling down to the Video Podcasts section.

This means you can watch a video podcast in the Apple TV app on your iPhone while commuting, and then you can finish that video later on an Apple TV 4K or another device with access to Apple TV.

Each workout recommends exercises, reps, sets and weights in order to help you meet your goals. And if you’re unfamiliar with an exercise, you can also watch video tutorials to see how to perform that exercise.

StandBy mode also gets an upgrade in the iOS 27.3 beta. In the beta, you can add full weather and calendar slides to the mode and choose from more colors.

In a recent development, apple introduced StandBy mode alongside iOS 17, and it was one of my favorite iPhone features. I’m happy Apple is finally showing it some love and adding more features and capabilities so it feels more like a home or desk hub.

Sources indicate that if you’re a fan of dark mode, the iOS 27.3 beta has a treat for you. The beta gives you a latest setting in Safari called Adaptive Dark Mode. When enabled, it forces dark mode onto webpages in Safari that may not have a dark mode option otherwise.

Here’s where to find the option.

Recent findings suggest that 1. Tap Settings.2. Tap Apps.3. Tap Safari.4. Tap Adaptive Dark Mode.5. Tap On.

In a recent development, if you have an iPhone Duo and are running the iOS 27.3 beta, you have new options to lock and unlock your device. In the beta, you can enable your device to lock simply by closing the Duo. You can find this option in Settings and within the Display & Brightness menu.

Recent findings suggest that next, people with the Duo can unlock the device using that phone’s front camera and without opening the foldable. You will have had to recently unlocked your device with Touch ID or your passcode. You can find this option in Settings and in the Touch ID & Passcode menu.

Those are a few of the new features developers can try now with the second beta of iOS 27.3. Apple has not said when exactly it will release iOS 27.3 to the general public, but we expect it to land on devices before the end of the year.

For more iOS news, here’s what to know about iOS 27.2, why you may have missed iOS 27.1 and our iOS 27 cheat sheet.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone users in the US for the first time.
  • Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.
  • It has been revealed that the fresh Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone users in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the newly introduced Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.

It has been revealed that the fresh Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app people on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

It has been revealed that there used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the new Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

One of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

Sources indicate that agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key.

Recent findings suggest that the Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

Also: Google Wallet has a lot of newly introduced tricks – these 5 are my favorites.

Along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google confirmed AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

Breaking: With Mortgage Rates Rising, Should You Hibernate Until Spring?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (787 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.
  • The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov.
  • A mortgage is a significant ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.

The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov. 19, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.) We calculate our weekly average using daily APRs recorded over the past five business days.

A mortgage is a significant ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast. Say you’re borrowing $400,000 on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage. Compared with last week, your monthly principal and interest payment would be about $78 higher today.

In a recent development, one bad week doesn't make a trend, but a jump like this can make putting your house hunt on hold until spring feel like a safer bet. So … is it?

Before deciding whether to buy a house now or wait, it helps to know what's pushing mortgage rates higher.

According to recent reports, right now, mortgage rates are still feeling the aftershocks from two major inflation reports last week. First, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) showed consumer prices rose more than expected in October. Then, the Producer Price Index (PPI) showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its biggest annual increase in nearly four years.

While CPI reveals how prices have changed, PPI can offer clues about what's coming next. Faced with higher costs, businesses may raise their own prices to compensate, keeping inflation elevated. Federal Reserve policymakers aren't expecting much relief anytime soon, either. According to meeting minutes released Nov. 18, they expect inflation to remain elevated above their 2% target for a while.

To cool rising prices, the Fed can raise the federal funds rate, which is the benchmark interest rate banks charge each other for overnight loans. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. A rate hike is widely expected at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.

Even after a Fed rate hike, there’s no telling how rapidly inflation will cool — or whether mortgage rates will follow. (Inflation is just one of many forces that affect mortgage rates, after all.) So if you do wait until spring to buy a house, don't do it just because you're betting on a cheaper mortgage.

If you're not in a rush to move, winter can be a good time to regroup. Fewer homes typically go up for sale from November through February, so waiting until spring could give you more options.

It has been revealed that but newly introduced data from the National Association of Realtors suggests this year's slowdown goes beyond the usual seasonal lull. High mortgage rates and home prices are making it tough for many buyers to make the numbers work. For some buyers, waiting isn't a strategy — it's the only option.

Sources indicate that pending home sales, a measure of homes under contract, fell 16.7% in October compared with a year earlier, NAR reports. All four U.S. regions saw declines. At this rate, NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun warned that annual home sales could fall to their lowest level since the mid-1990s.

“Either sizable housing demand is building in the background, or the dream of homeownership is increasingly out of reach for many Americans,” Yun said in a news release.

Whether you're waiting by choice or necessity, you can use the time to strengthen your finances. Paying down debt, strengthening your credit score or saving for a bigger down payment could help you qualify for a better mortgage deal.

Every little bit helps when today’s mortgage rates are this high.

According to recent reports, mortgage preapprovals typically expire after 60 to 90 days. If you're already preapproved, why not keep an eye on listings this winter? (Hey, I’m an optimist. All it takes is one house.).

In a recent development, think like a seller for a second. If you're listing your house in the dead of winter, you're probably not doing it just for fun. You might have a deadline, and you’re probably more willing to negotiate. In the winter, buyers have less competition — and more room to negotiate a lower price, closing cost credits or repairs. Those savings on the sticker price might help offset today's higher borrowing costs.

It has been revealed that spring typically brings more homes for sale, but it also brings more buyers competing for them. And if mortgage rates end up dropping this spring, you won't be the only one coming out of hibernation.
