💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider.
  • New data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.
  • According to recent reports, also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider. At the same time, they’re turning to AI to help screen more candidates — meaning those videos you’ve seen on the internet of people pranking AI interviewers aren’t going away anytime soon.

New data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.

According to recent reports, also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI? This dashboard tracks the cuts – and the cost.

“The survey data is self-reported, so it reflects what employers believe has happened, not a measured outcome,” Greenhouse’s Head of Voice AI Ophir Samson told ZDNET via email.

According to recent reports, employers are also reacting to AI by adjusting their hiring processes: 86% of those surveyed reported changes to account for AI’s impact. 57% of them did so by adding another human interview.

Industry observers note that “As jobseekers rely more on AI to polish and send out their job applications, employers are finding it harder to tell who’s actually right for the role,” the report stated, echoing an ongoing push-and-pull between applicants and hiring teams. AI resume screeners automatically toss a majority of applications they deem unfit, so applicants try not to get tossed by formatting their material for the screener, which then backfires anyway.

The report reveals how a tough economy and an influx of AI hiring tools are colliding, arguably to benefit employers over applicants. Greenhouse noted that, ironically, AI tools are helping hiring managers while also making resumes untrustworthy, and applicants would rather be interviewed by AI than not at all.

Also: How to beat the AI algorithm and get the job of your dreams.

“A growing number of employers are using AI not just to filter candidates out, but to have conversations with more candidates, earlier, through AI-powered voice technology,” Greenhouse said, adding that “half now use AI interviews to hear from more candidates, and 40% of those have found strong candidates they would have missed.”.

Greenhouse itself offers a voice AI screening interview tool. Samson told ZDNET that an HR professional ran 200 candidates she’d rejected through Greenhouse’s tool, and it suggested 19.

“All five of the finalists came from that group, and she ultimately hired one from the group,” Samson said.

Recent findings suggest that what we don’t, and maybe can’t, know is the inverse: whether AI screeners influence hiring managers to turn away candidates they actually should have considered. At least in Greenhouse’s case, Samson stated Voice AI doesn’t make hiring decisions or “automatically advance, reject, or rank candidates.”.

“Recruiters review every output, and one recruiter owns the outcome and can explain how they reached it,” he noted.

Greenhouse’s report surveyed 1,347 hiring managers and recruiters across the US, UK, Germany, Australia, and Ireland from late September to mid-October, and found that half of employers using voice AI “say the early-stage candidate experience has improved.”.

Also: ‘So perfect, they are literally identical’ – Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ new top stressor.

Recent findings suggest that it’s unclear what “improved” means there, though, and whether applicants themselves would agree with that. Still, when given the choice, only 7% of applicants in the US would turn down an AI interview, per an earlier Greenhouse report. Additionally, “70% of those who’ve had a live AI interview say it helped them show their skills,” that report remarked.

Sources indicate that but how swayed is that by the state of the US job market? October’s job report was better than expected, but it’s still been a tough year overall for job-seekers. Greenhouse’s findings could be as much a reflection of how desperate applicants are as an endorsement of or comfort with AI screenings.

Recent findings suggest that “The job market could be a factor. Our Future of Hiring Candidate Report shows 81% of job seekers were rejected from a job in the past year without speaking to anyone at the organization, human or AI,” Samson remarked. “But I’d be careful about reading the data as desperation. Candidates are setting clear conditions: nearly half (49%) want to know if a human will review their responses and 40% want to know how they’ll be evaluated.”.

Also: Why replacing staff with AI backfires – and 5 ways smart leaders generate real value instead.

Recent findings suggest that samson said that a software engineer named Ryan Quinlan, who was hired at Blissway, initially thought “talking to an AI” sounded stranger, but that it ultimately “felt like a conversation” that let him mention skills he’d forgotten to include on his resume. Samson said that Ryan has been “a ‘maybe’ on paper,” but that the AI interview helped him get over the line to be considered.

In a recent development, “For most applicants, a human conversation was never on the table,” Samson said. “The real choice is a resume lost in a pile, or 15 minutes to tell their story.”.

Greenhouse found that while employers are using AI to screen more candidates, most are maintaining human oversight over the most important decisions in the hiring process.

“Of all the tasks employers would hand to an AI agent, deciding which candidates to advance came last, at just 7%,” Greenhouse said.

A recent California law aims to protect employees from being fired by AI systems that make determinations about their performance without a human co-signing the assessment. As with many AI productivity tools in the workplace, proper adoption ideally equates to more time for human workers to handle more crucial tasks.

Also: 92% of HR say staff can train for AI jobs – but half of companies still hire outside.

“Of employers who’ve saved time with AI, 85% put it back into candidates, most often by spending more time with shortlisted candidates (45%) and interviewing more candidates earlier (40%),” Greenhouse said.

The main question around AI interviewers remains whether they’re correctly capturing your interview the way you’d hope a human interviewer would (though that’s still deeply subjective and out of applicants’ control anyway).

“When AI interviews are implemented thoughtfully and transparently, they pay off for both candidates and recruiters,” Samson stated. “Every candidate who uses our Voice AI can opt out, and about 90% rate the experience as excellent.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you use an AI chatbot and you’re concerned about your privacy and the personal information it ingests, you can do something about it. While Claude — our top pick for AI chatbots — is one of the better options when it comes to privacy, the default settings can still leave something to be desired if you value yours.

Luckily, you can mitigate or even eliminate the amount of data Claude knows about you, as long as you know where to look.

From having Claude train on your conversations to track your location and more, here are a series of settings you should consider changing if you want to stay on top of your privacy when using one of the best AI chatbots around.

By default, most AI chatbots have a setting on by default that allows them to be trained on the conversations you have. This is the first and likely the most crucial setting you need to disable. Here’s how to turn it off.

The settings essentially remain the same across web, iOS and Android:.

You may not see this option because with some accounts, like Enterprise plans, Claude doesn’t automatically collect this data. So if you have a Claude account through work, you might not have to worry about this.

While you’re at it, if you’re a Claude Code user, these settings will let you delete Code sessions stored on Anthropic’s server without deleting local sessions on your computer.

If you’ve ever shared a chat with anyone, you can also delete those chats in this menu as well.

Read More: Keep Your Data Yours: How to Opt Out of AI Chatbot Training.

Anthropic will use your location when using Claude to “improve product experience.” It will use your device’s IP address to identify your city and region, but you can disable this setting — to some extent. How you go about doing this will depend on what device you’re using to access Claude.

Sources indicate that according to the support article, if you’re using the mobile app (iOS or Android) or the web extension, the location settings are located within the device’s settings and not the Claude app settings. However, I found two ways to do this on Android. (See below.).

The Claude app will not request access to your location unless your prompt has a specific location-based query, like “What are some of the best sushi restaurants around me?” Only then will the app request permission.

However, if you already have given Claude access on Android or iOS, here’s how you can revoke permission.

I was surprised to see a section in the Settings of the Android app that I didn’t see on iOS, but it will also allow you to disable your location right from the app.

One thing to keep in mind is that turning your location off can affect features like searches that require your location, but Anthropic explicitly states that it collects your IP address to infer coarse-grained location to ensure usage of Claude complies with its terms and to prevent abuse — despite questionable allegations.

Recent findings suggest that like other AI chatbots, Claude has built-in “memory” so it can more easily have context about your conversations. Memory is on by default: The chatbot will remember personal preferences and other information and will be able to take that into consideration in other conversations, even if you don’t explicitly mention it in your current session.

If you’d prefer a clean slate, you can ask in the chat what memories it has collected about you and then tell Claude to delete specific memories or all of them. However, there’s a dedicated section in the settings to help you view and manage memories directly.

In the web version of Claude, do the following to access your memory settings:.

According to recent reports, this will display all stored memories Claude has for you. You can edit a specific memory to your liking by clicking on the pencil icon on the right side of the memory or delete it entirely by clicking on the trash icon.

To prevent Claude from creating upcoming memories from your conversations:.

If you have had conversations with Claude that were sensitive in nature and still had the “Help improve our AI models” option enabled, odds are that Anthropic has already trained Claude on that conversation. There’s no way to change that.

However, you should find those conversations in your chat history and delete them. After you’ve done that and disabled AI training on your conversations, you should opt for incognito mode for any further sensitive conversations you might want to have going forward.

Incognito chats aren’t saved in your history, nor are they used to train models.

The Flipper One crowdfunding campaign has broken the $13-million mark, smashing the funding raised for previous Flipper devices and demonstrating strong interest in the successor to the Flipper Zero. The $399 Flipper One is a pocket Linux computer focused on networking, with delivery estimated for July 2027. But it isn’t simply an updated version of the Flipper Zero. It’s a very different animal and a much more serious bit of kit.

Industry observers note that the thing that made the Flipper Zero so popular was how easy it was to use. You could fire it up and turn the volume down on the TV at your parents’ place, see the radio waves coming from your car’s key fob, and copy hotel room key cards.

Also: The Flipper One may be the ultimate Linux PC for hackers in 2026 – and I’m excited.

According to recent reports, it could do a lot, there wasn’t a steep learning curve, and you didn’t need to buy anything else. Did the fake videos on TikTok from people claiming they could change the prices at gas stations (I wish!) or start cars remotely help make the Zero more popular?

Unfortunately, yes. But what made it successful was that it packed a lot of power into a package that was small, fun, affordable, and easy to use.

If the Flipper Zero, with its NFC, RFID, sub-GHz, and IR, was kindergarten, the Flipper One is a college degree: a pocket Linux computer focused on networking.

This is reflected in the price. You can pick up a Zero for $169, while the Flipper One is $399.

What this buys you is the Flipper One base computer with a 256 × 144 grayscale LCD, Rockchip RK3576 8-core ARM SoC with NPU, a low-power MCU for handling the LCD and user interface, 8GB of LPDDR5 RAM, 64GB of UFS 2.2 storage, and a microSD slot.

If that $399 feels like a lot, it’s worth keeping in mind that, according to Flipper, the price only covers production costs and that the RAM and UFS storage account for at least half of the total hardware cost.

If you think this is a lot, you could spend a lot more. Adding a LoRa, SDR, or 5G module will push the total up a lot higher. And if you want all three modules, you’re looking at $759 for the Flipper One Ultimate Bundle.

Also: The Flipper One is the Linux cyberdeck I wish my Raspberry Pi could be.

The reception has been strong enough that pledges have flown past the $300,000 goal that Flipper initially set, with over 24,000 backers pledging over $13 million. Close to 5,300 backers have gone for the Ultimate Bundle, compared to just over 4,300 choosing the bare Flipper One.

This suggests that backers really want the radio capabilities that this latest platform offers.

If you want one, this crowdfunding run is a good time to get one because it’s a Kickstarter Special slashing 25% off an estimated retail price of $550.

The response over on Reddit has been a little more subdued, with some being taken aback by the price of the Zero’s bigger sibling.

Also: 7 useful things I can do with my Flipper Zero – as someone who’s used it for years.

As someone who homebrews a lot of electronics, I’m going to say that the price is justified, and this project goes far beyond something you could put together with a Raspberry Pi and some code.

Sources indicate that the Flipper One campaign runs until Dec. 17, 2026, with delivery estimated for July 2027.

It has been revealed that keep in mind that this is a Kickstarter pledge, not a purchase, and that rewards aren’t guaranteed. Flipper also states on the Kickstarter page that component shortages are the biggest risk to the project and that they “could cause significant delays to production and delivery.” It also says that if RAM prices continue to rise, it cannot “rule out adjusting some product specifications, including reducing the amount of RAM.”.

Also: Is the Flipper Zero the best multi-tool for hacking?

And the good news here is that I’ve seen several analysts predicting that RAM prices will begin to go down in 2027 as demand eases off.

Recent findings suggest that meta promised to be carbon-neutral and water-positive by 2030 — that is, the company would offset as much carbon dioxide as it created and return more water to local watersheds than it used. But like every Massive Tech company, Meta is sacrificing its climate goals for artificial intelligence and the data centers needed to run it.

In Meta’s 2026 sustainability report, released on Thursday, Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the company is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline … We’ll continue to invest in emissions reductions.”.

Sources indicate that it’s a disappointing, if unsurprising, announcement. Microsoft, Amazon and Google have also all backtracked on their climate goals in their rush to build hyperscale data centers, the turbocharged server farms needed to keep AI online. Microsoft’s president, Brad Smith, said in 2023 that the manufacturer’s net zero goal was “before the explosion in artificial intelligence.”.

According to recent reports, meta’s net emissions in 2025 were 11.8 million metric tons of carbon dioxide, a 45% increase year over year, the tech giant says. Carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases are primary drivers of the climate crisis, worsening natural disasters, causing more extreme weather patterns and disrupting the lives of everyone and everything on the planet.

Take one of Meta’s Louisiana data centers, Hyperion, for example. CEO Mark Zuckerberg unveiled the behemoth in 2025, showing how the facility is nearly the size of Manhattan. When it comes online in 2030, it’s expected to create two gigawatts of capacity for AI, with the ability to scale in the future. But it also requires equally massive demands on the state’s energy grid.

Meta details in length its strategies for mitigating the environmental impact of its work, including improved water-use efficiencies in its data centers and approximately 77% less embodied carbon in its newly introduced data center designs compared to its original ones.

But, again, AI has made an indelible mark on those efforts. The company also reports that its electricity consumption “increased 35% year over year as additional data centers came online.”.

Meta wrote that “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.” Arguably, as one of the biggest hyperscalers driving the buildout of AI infrastructure here in the US and abroad, Meta should have known.

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that don’t ask your AI agent to read and decipher that lengthy text message.
  • According to recent reports, the privacy-focused messaging and calling app is rolling out a new default setting to stop built-in smartphone AI agents from potentially seeing and saving your Signal data.
  • That threatens Signal’s mission to guarantee privacy, Whittaker wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that don’t ask your AI agent to read and decipher that lengthy text message. And don’t screenshot it either. It may seem harmless, but Signal’s latest setting underlines that it isn’t.

According to recent reports, the privacy-focused messaging and calling app is rolling out a new default setting to stop built-in smartphone AI agents from potentially seeing and saving your Signal data. In a blog post announcing the change, Signal President Meredith Whittaker said these AI bots scan what’s on your screen to get to know you, capturing your data and making it available to AI systems to fulfill your requests, such as answering questions you may ask.

That threatens Signal’s mission to guarantee privacy, Whittaker wrote. So it’s putting a stop to it with a default setting to block screenshots in the Signal app on iOS 27 and when AI assistants try to capture information on Android screens by default.

Whittaker stated that this isn’t the first time Signal has taken such measures against an operating system. Last year, it blocked screenshots of Signal messages from Microsoft’s Recall AI on Windows 11.

Now the company is taking a similar approach to Apple’s iOS 27 and Android operating systems, where AI assistants try to read your Signal screen.

Industry observers note that the problem is the same for the three major OS companies. Microsoft, Google and Apple are incorporating AI into their operating systems, and Signal says that compromises the space for third-party developers, including Signal, to build apps for these systems.

“Right now, these agentic AI integrations are changing this environment in a way that’s making it increasingly hostile to privacy,” Whittaker wrote.

It has been revealed that whittaker noted the screenshot setting won’t fix everything, because AI agents can still sneakily access data on your phone. Tech companies should take steps to give developers more choice, such as an opt-out to disable AI agent access, and provide more documentation on how big tech AI agents work.

Sources indicate that “Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience,” Whittaker noted. “This is also the reason we are currently unable to implement these protections on MacOS.”.

In most cases, text messages are encrypted when they travel between devices. But AI agents can bypass that. John Strand, CEO of Black Hills Information Security, explained that when you access the information, it has to be decrypted because you cannot read encrypted data.

Recent findings suggest that “So, if an AI agent can access screenshots or directly observe what’s happening on your screen, it can read those messages without ever having to break the encryption itself,” said Strand. “That’s the scary part. You can have incredibly strong encryption, but if something can see what the user sees, that encryption isn’t going to protect you at that point.”.

If you want to take screenshots in Signal, you can disable the setting, but that could mean AI agents could access you and your senders’ information, like text messages and shared files such as photos.

Strand remarked the worst-case scenario is that an attacker could see everything you see, from private conversations to passwords. And that’s what Signal is trying to avoid.

“They want to make sure that if something like this happens, they’ve done absolutely everything they reasonably can to protect their customers and the information being accessed through their application,” Strand stated.

Signal, Apple and Google did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Also: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI training.

Latest to Google’s AI Mode is an option known as temporary threads. By choosing this setting, any searches you conduct in AI mode are detached from your own Google account and history. Your temporary searches won’t be affected by your past preferences or chats. They won’t be impacted by any personalization you’ve set up through your account. And they won’t be saved to your chat history. The goal here is to prevent anyone else, including Google, from accessing your conversations in this mode.

This option is presently rolling out around the world in all languages to Google search on both desktop and mobile browsers. You can run a temporary thread on any device and in any browser.

Recent findings suggest that try this for yourself: Head to the regular Google search page and click the button on the search field for AI Mode. You should then see an icon with a pen hovering over a dotted circle. If you don’t see it, you may have to run a search to get started. On the results page, you should then spot the icon.

Industry observers note that hover over the icon, and the tooltip will say: “Start temporary thread.” Click the icon on the left to start a upcoming thread. Now, any conversation you kick off will be temporary and unconnected to your account. But you don’t have to stick with just plain old text. Select the plus icon to upload an image or file. Select the microphone icon to speak instead of type.

Also: Goodbye, Gemini Gems: How to use Google’s new Skills.

It has been revealed that certain limitations are in effect with a temporary thread. Specifically, you can’t do any of the following:.

Are these temporary threads truly private? Here’s what Google notes:.

“Temporary threads will not be saved to your Google account and disappear after 24 hours,” Google said on a support page. “They won’t be used to train Google’s generative AI models, unless you submit feedback or it’s necessary for safety purposes. Google will still collect data and use data that is not associated with your account, including to keep our services working smoothly and safely and to support business operations.”.

Google also warns that your browser may still save your history if you visit a website within a temporary thread. Data could still be collected by the sites you visit and the services those sites use, including Google services like Google Analytics.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

For those reasons, you should still be cautious about the information you share even in a temporary thread. But certainly, this option provides greater privacy and protection than a regular AI Mode search.

It has been revealed that chatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot all offer a temporary chat mode that also promises to keep your chats private and unconnected to your account. Claude and Perplexity provide the same feature but call it incognito mode.

Recent findings suggest that I’m glad to see Google finally offering this option through its AI Mode searches. This marks the second privacy-friendly development in recent days from the search giant. #16493. Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Officially Heading to Mars

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (772 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Officially Heading to Mars

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (772 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, NASA rolled out its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars.
  • It has been revealed that it’s an exciting time for NASA.
  • According to recent reports, typically, spacecraft use a planet or the sun’s natural gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, NASA rolled out its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars. After spending a year looping near Earth, the twin probes completed a gravity-assist maneuver this month and are now en route to the red planet.

It has been revealed that it’s an exciting time for NASA. Blue and Gold, named for the school colors of UC Berkeley where they were built, completed the agency’s first powered Earth flyby.

According to recent reports, typically, spacecraft use a planet or the sun’s natural gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance. A notable example is Voyager 1, which used unpowered gravity-assisted flybys to reach the speeds needed to cross the light-day threshold earlier this week. Escapade did this with Earth’s gravity but also used thrusters to generate even more speed. Since there are two of them, NASA personnel had to perform this maneuver twice.

The other significant win for NASA is that Mars will soon have two additional satellites in orbit to measure the planet’s magnetosphere, which is believed to have been stripped by the solar wind eons ago, when the planet likely had liquid water.

Sources indicate that these satellites are notable for being NASA’s first low-cost mission to Mars, costing the agency approximately $75 million as part of the Small Innovative Missions for Planetary Exploration program. It also marked the official debut of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket for a space mission, and the firm was able to achieve the first vertical landing of its rocket after sending Escapade on its way.

Sources indicate that escapade still has a long way to go. Blue and Gold are now spending the next 10 months flying into outer space. Their new trajectory is set to take them into Mars’ orbital path, timed in such a way that the twin satellites will arrive at the same time that Mars naturally shows up, allowing the red planet to capture the twins in its orbit as it flies by. NASA says that both are set to arrive at Mars by early September next year.

By the time the twins get there, they will have been in space for 22 months. Flights to Mars require months of deep space travel, impeccable timing and loads of fuel. However, if missions hit specific launch windows, they require far less fuel.

Industry observers note that this is a well-documented maneuver known as the Hohmann Transfer, and NASA’s JPL has a neat math exercise to show how it’s calculated. NASA intentionally launched Escapade a year early so that the satellites could hang out in a gravitational sweet spot called the L2 Earth-Sun Lagrange point. This is a point in space on the side of the Earth opposite the sun, and the idea was to have the spacecraft already in orbit and ready for the next Mars launch window.

Once it opened, the satellites engaged their thrusters, performed a gravity-assisted flyby of Earth to gain speed, and introduced themselves into outer space.

The tactic of sending Escapade to the L2 Lagrange point to wait for a Mars window to open is arguably NASA’s biggest win, as no space agency has ever attempted it. The benefit is that it allows agencies to launch payloads into orbit bound for Mars whenever they have the time, then use Earth gravity assists to slingshot them out to Mars when it’s most efficient.

“With this loiter orbit and Earth flyby, Escapade is pioneering a upcoming strategy for getting to Mars,” Jeff Parker, CTO of Advanced Space and lead mission designer, said in a statement. “This method provides the flexibility to launch almost anytime and then use Earth’s gravity to get a boost to Mars, rather than waiting every two years to launch there directly when the planets are aligned.”.

It has been revealed that the maneuver paid dividends. JAXA, Japan’s national space agency, launched its MMX spacecraft on Oct. 20, which is within the current Mars launch window and employs the same Hohmann Transfer method to get to Mars. The spacecraft is headed to Phobos and Deimos, Mars’s moons.

Sources indicate that despite using the more traditional method of waiting for the window to open to launch, JAXA’s MMX is slated to reach its destination in August next year, just a couple of weeks ahead of Escapade. When you factor in that Escapade performed its gravity-assist slingshot on Nov. 9, roughly two weeks before MMX launched, the spacecraft will reach their respective destinations in approximately the same amount of time, validating NASA’s trajectory strategy.

Linux is all about choice. From the kernel all the way up to the desktop environment, you get to determine what is used and even how it is used. The staggering number of distributions, desktops, package managers, file managers, and terminal apps provide you with a nearly infinite combination of choices. That choice is and has always been a key aspect of Linux.

Industry observers note that so too is innovation. If there’s one thing that separates Linux from all other operating systems, it’s the willingness to try something different. Linux developers are always pushing the limits of what an operating system is, and this new take on the OS is the epitome of that.

It has been revealed that the distribution in question is called Pond. According to the developers, “Pond is an opportunity for us to play with familiar conventions and experiment with new ideas that make a computer more natural and satisfying.”.

Industry observers note that the developers have achieved something special. Pond takes the standard UI and turns it on its head. Part tiling window manager, part mobile UI, part GNOME, and part something we’ve never before seen, this desktop environment is special. It took me all of five minutes to fall in love with what they’ve created.

The Pond UI consists of the following:.

Also: The only 4 Linux email clients I recommend.

It has been revealed that if you’ve ever considered using a tiling window manager, but thought the lack of a mouse made it seem a bit too complicated, Pond is exactly what you want. Here’s how it works:.

It has been revealed that pond uses the Niri window manager to arrange windows in columns along an infinite strip from left to right. In multi-monitor setups, each display gets its own strip, so windows never “overflow” from one monitor to the next.

Also: How to install Arch Linux without losing your mind.

At the same time, workspaces are dynamic, and there’s always a fresh workspace automatically created to the right of the farthest-right window. The combination of the Pond sidebar and Niri’s way of handling windows makes this UI truly original.

In a recent development, pond doesn’t have a traditional desktop menu. Instead, you open the launcher (using the Super+Space key combination), type the name of the app you want to install, and hit Enter when the app name appears on both the display and as an icon in the top portion of the sidebar.

Another thing that sets Pond apart is how you install apps. Yes, you can open a terminal window and install an app using the pacman command, or you can open the launcher, type install, press Enter, and then type the name of the app you want to install. For instance, if you wanted to install LibreOffice, you would type:.

Sources indicate that once you hit Enter a second time, the installation will begin. Many apps install via Flatpak, but on the off-chance an app must be installed via the pacman package manager, you’ll be prompted to type your user password before the installation begins.

Sources indicate that as I hinted earlier, Pond is based on Arch Linux, which means it’s a rolling-release distribution. One matter that did give me pause was the lack of a GUI update system, which indicates that updates would have to happen in the terminal, like so:.

I installed the Shelly GUI frontend, which does have an upgrade component. Personally, I would simply open the terminal window, type sudo pacman -Syu, hit Enter, and let the update run in the background. But if a GUI is your jam, Shelly is what you want.

Also: A super fast distro for anyone ready to move beyond beginner Linux.

It would be sweet if the developers allowed updating the system from within the launcher, so it didn’t require opening the terminal first. The Pond launcher does allow running system commands from the launcher, which will then open the terminal window and execute the command. For instance, open the terminal, type a command, hit Enter, and then scroll through the list of available commands that can be run.

Pond ships with kernel 7.3.4-3, so it has outstanding hardware recognition and performance.

According to recent reports, you should definitely give Pond a try, especially if you’re adventurous and want to experience something completely different. If, on the other hand, different is not in your stream, then Pond will frustrate you to no end.

Also: Why Nextcloud Office is my latest favorite free productivity suite.

According to recent reports, pond excited me more than any OS has in a very long time; so much so that I could see this becoming my go-to OS, once it reaches stable release. Until then, I will keep Pond installed on a laptop, keep upgrading, and see what happens next.

Kudos to the Pond OS team for coming up with something truly unique in an already competitive world.

Industry observers note that hilton is making a significant play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort. The massive 1,000-room property — which underwent an $80 million renovation before opening under the Signia Hilton brand in May 2026 — sits on the beach in Hollywood, Florida, just outside of Fort Lauderdale.

Sources indicate that the resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R. The main downside: The location isn’t great if your trip primarily revolves around off-property excursions, dining and nightlife.

According to recent reports, room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable. There’s also a resort fee of $59 per night — but Hilton waives that when you book using Hilton points.

Hilton covered the cost of my stay for two nights, but the opinions in this review are my own. Here’s what guests can expect at this oceanfront resort.

Since the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort is part of Hilton Honors, there are several ways to book a stay there.

If you’re using Hilton points, expect to pay 70,000 to 80,000 points a night when standard rooms are available. Hilton elite status — a benefit you can earn by holding any Hilton Honors credit card — gets you the fifth-night-free perk, where you stay for at least five nights but pay for four when booking with points.

For example, if you were to stay five nights at 80,000 points a night, you’d pay 320,000 points total, bringing down your average nightly rate to 64,000 points.

It has been revealed that you can also book using Hilton’s generous free night certificates, which can be used at almost any property in the portfolio. If you hold the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card, you automatically get a certificate each year. It’s also possible to earn certificates through reaching spending thresholds on the card and on the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass® Card. Terms apply.

Make sure to check the cash rate against the points rate to make sure you’re getting good value from your redemption. NerdWallet values Hilton points at 0.4 cent apiece.

For cash bookings of two nights or more, you might consider using The Hotel Collection via American Express’ travel portal for eligible cardholders. Eligible bookings come with benefits like a $100 property credit and other amenities subject to availability, including a room upgrade, early check-in and late checkout.

Keep in mind that third-party bookings typically don’t earn Hilton points or count toward elite status qualification.

It’s hard to miss the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort, with its signature H-shaped facade and sleek white-and-glass exterior.

Recent findings suggest that stepping into the hotel, I was immediately struck by the lush greenery filling the entrance and indoor courtyard. The grand lobby has soaring glass ceilings, giving the space a greenhouse feel, although the strong air conditioning keeps you cool.

Despite its massive size, it doesn’t have a sprawling layout, which I appreciated. Everything is close together, and you can walk from the check-in counter to any of the indoor restaurants in under a minute.

In a recent development, I stayed in an oceanfront suite with a balcony, which was spacious and had a fun beachy vibe. To get to the rooms, you’ll need to use either the north or south tower elevator banks.

In the living room, there was a large sitting area featuring a TV, a couch, an accent chair and a four-person high-top table.

Although I didn’t spend too much time on the balcony — the October balminess was a bit too much for me — I enjoyed stepping out each morning to admire the view.

The bedroom had a king bed with extremely comfortable bedding and an oversized chair that was a great spot to relax and read a book by the window.

The bathroom was spacious, featuring a shower and a separate tub (something every room has).

In a recent development, even the standard room I toured felt roomy. I liked that it shared similar elements with the suite, including the oversized lounge chair.

This is what you’d normally get when booking a room at the cheapest points price.

According to recent reports, there are several dining venues on the property, ranging from a grab-and-go cafe to a high-end steakhouse. It is a luxury resort, so expect the prices to reflect that.

Sources indicate that for breakfast, you can head to Palmea Kitchen, which is also open for lunch. I had the breakfast buffet, which offered a nice spread of classics, from hot food items and pastries to cold cuts and smoked salmon.

If you don’t have time for a sit-down breakfast, you can head next door to The Press, which offers made-to-order and grab-and-go food options throughout the day. You can also get smoothies, juices, snacks, pastries and other sweet treats.

The Canteen is another grab-and-go option that also sells snacks, drinks, souvenirs and sundries, similar to a convenience store.

It has been revealed that for lunch and dinner, try Solara. It doesn’t have a traditional restaurant feel, as it’s mostly an indoor-outdoor bar space. One side connects to the lobby, while the other side faces the Solara adults-only pool.

It serves a lunch menu, as well as a substantial bar food menu that’s available late into the night.

In a recent development, you can also eat at Playa Beach Bar & Grill, a beachside restaurant serving Latin-inspired cuisine. I enjoyed spending a lazy lunch there and watching the waves crash onto the shore.

For a fancy sit-down dinner, go to Diplomat Prime, the property’s steakhouse. We had a group dinner at the restaurant, and the meats were, of course, the highlight. But don’t sleep on the seafood, which was also delicious.

One of the best parts of the Dip, as it’s affectionately known, is its location right on the beach. Guests can access the stretch of beach directly adjacent to the property. But it’s not a private beach, so you might encounter crowds.

I didn’t spend any time on the beach itself — it was extremely windy while I was there — but the hotel’s resort fee includes amenities like a beach lounge (umbrella not included), a daily one-hour kayak or paddleboard rental, and beachfront yoga classes.

If you don’t want to get sand everywhere, you can head to one of the three pool options: the adults-only Solara pool, the family-friendly lagoon pool and the Verandah Social Club for those 21 and older (requires paid access).

It has been revealed that the family-friendly lagoon spans the length of the property and runs beneath the Solara pool. It also has its own hot tub.

I spent an afternoon in a cabana at the Verandah Social Club, which has some smaller plunge pools and a hot tub.

I appreciated the attentive service from the staff there, who constantly checked on whether guests needed anything.

If you’re looking for other ways to stay active, head to the two-story fitness center, featuring a variety of equipment like free weights, exercise bikes, a rowing machine and treadmills.

Recent findings suggest that next door, you’ll find the spa and wellness center. I had a relaxing massage that incorporated hot stones and aromatherapy.

The locker rooms come with a sauna and steam room, although I wished there were more amenities like a hot tub and cold plunge.

One of the resort fee inclusions is complimentary high-intensity interval training workout classes at the gym across the street. I signed up for an early morning class. The instructor was friendly, and it was a great way to start my day.

Other amenities include a complimentary one-hour e-bike rental each day, as well as a kids’ club with various activities (but drop-off fees apply).

I had a fantastic stay at this resort, but I’d recommend it for a specific traveler.

Sources indicate that if you’re planning to stay on-property your entire trip, it’s a great option. That’s probably why it’s such a popular convention hotel, since everything you need is easily accessible.

I loved the hotel’s design, including the jungle-like atmosphere in the lobby, and I found the dining options to be tasty, albeit pricey.

But if your trip revolves around visiting Miami attractions, you’ll likely want to stay closer to the action.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta’s Muse AI agent has only been around for a few months, but already has a track record of user privacy violations. Even Meta employees are reporting concerning incidents, including the agent taking actions they didn’t ask it to and sharing information they didn’t recognize that appears to belong to other users.

Also: Don’t use Muse? Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

According to a Reuters investigation, Meta employees testing Muse remarked the agent messaged them about topics they hadn’t asked it about, including career advice, a follow-up on a request for childcare, products they hadn’t purchased, and, crucially, bank account balances they didn’t recognize.

These incidents “prompted unnerved employees to raise concerns it could be mixing up conversations between different accounts and exposing customers’ private data,” Reuters mentioned.

Reuters said “an employee told colleagues his Muse had randomly added an extra message to its regular chats about fishing-related weather and tide information, saying: ‘BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2,722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5,899.57.'” In another instance, Muse booked a non-refundable Airbnb for an employee who hadn’t instructed it to.

Muse notified another employee, who was using the agent on her personal phone, about a message she’d received on Signal, though she remarked she hadn’t given the agent access to the encrypted messaging app.

Also: Meta Muse is the worst AI agent for privacy – and I’ve tried them all.

Reuters and the AI Now Institute determined, through testing on an Android phone and a Mac, that Muse used “permissions granted during the bot’s initial setup to pull in the message text, leveraging those authorizations in ways a user might not anticipate.” Because Muse is set up with automatic access to Android push notifications, it didn’t need explicit app access to read messages.

The tests did not work on an iPhone, suggesting better protections against Muse’s prying.

In a recent development, similarly, in September, a user reported Muse had shared his address with a Facebook Marketplace buyer before checking with him. The incident was ultimately a misunderstanding between the terms the user thought he’d consented to and how much access he was actually handing over, which exemplifies that Meta and the user may have explicitly different definitions of access, and that Muse can take advantage of that grey area.

Meta told Reuters these incidents were either isolated or the result of hallucinations, though Reuters could not confirm that.

In a recent development, these are just the latest in a string of alarming incidents surrounding Muse. In its first month, a cybersecurity professional discovered Muse had a serious zero-day bug that made it hijackable. At least one journalist found the AI sifting through his Apple Messages after he’d explicitly denied those permissions, which Apple then issued stronger privacy protections to address. Banks have also blocked agents over concerns.

It has been revealed that as a firm, Meta doesn’t have a solid history of respecting user privacy. That legacy is partly what informed ZDNET contributor David Gewirtz’s suspicion of the AI assistant when he tested it, though it earned his assigned title of “worst AI agent for privacy” all on its own. The agent asked him for everything from contacts and chats to his logins and passwords, and Meta automatically uses conversations with Muse to train its AI.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac.

It has been revealed that public awareness of the risks of AI agents hit a peak last year with the viral OpenClaw. The predominant advice for using agents has been to take every privacy precaution: Be careful with the data you share and the apps you give it permissions for, and watch what you tell it. But if customers believe they’re doing so by restricting access to certain apps, just for Muse to find a way in anyway, privacy hygiene isn’t enough.

Also: How to keep your chatbot conversations as private as possible.

Reuters’ findings may provide an opportunity for Google’s agentic offering, now called Tasks (formerly Spark), which it made free (with usage limits, like Muse) this week.

By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 20, 2026 at 3:36PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Revolution Medicines ›.

Revolution Medicines (RVMD +1.11%) is living up to its name. Earlier this year, the biotech company earned approval for Rasonque, a medicine for pancreatic cancer that targets one of the main genetic drivers of the disease, the first of its kind to do so. Rasonque's approval was a major milestone, and Revolution Medicines has already been rewarded for it. Shares are up 100% this year. Is there any upside left for the drugmaker?

Many new drugs are tested against a placebo in Phase 3 clinical trials. Being pitted against the standard of care is a much tougher bar to clear. Yet, that's exactly what Rasonque did. In a Phase 3 study, investigators pitted the medicine against cytotoxic chemotherapy, the current standard of care, in patients with previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer.

Industry observers note that rasonque won hands down. It led to a median overall survival of 13.2 months, compared with 6.7 months with cytotoxic chemotherapy. Why is Rasonque so effective? It has a newly introduced mechanism of action that targets RAS-addicted cancers (RAS is a protein implicated in the rapid growth of some cancers), which have historically been difficult to treat.

Recent findings suggest that according to Revolution Medicines, RAS-addicted cancers account for between 20% and 30% of all human cancers. So, the manufacturer could earn approval for Rasonque and some other candidates in its pipeline across various indications. Revolution Medicines is running eight Phase 3 clinical trials, including several for two other investigational medicines, zoldonrasib and elironrasib. Provided Rasonque experiences a strong commercial ramp-up, and the company makes significant clinical progress over the next few years, Revolution Medicines' shares could maintain strong momentum.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Rasonque earned approval in late August. Yet, in the third quarter, Revolution Medicines generated $198 million in revenue from the medicine, in the roughly five weeks it was on the market before the quarter ended. It was prescribed to more than 5,000 unique patients in the U.S. Some analysts are calling it the strongest launch in the history of the oncology drug market, which is typically dominated by pharmaceutical leaders.

That's impressive, and it highlights the massive opportunity Revolution Medicines is tapping into. That helps put Revolution Medicines' valuation in perspective. The company's current market cap is $34.8 billion, which is quite high for a biotech company that just launched its first product. However, note that Revolution Medicines' stock has declined about 29% since Rasonque's approval, even as the company's initial launch of the drug has crushed expectations.

If anything, Revolution Medicines' third-quarter results show that the market cap it had several months ago, which hovered around $50 billion, may not have been unfounded after all. Consider that some analysts now expect the organization to generate $3 billion in revenue next year. Based on this projection, Revolution Medicines is trading at 11.6x estimated 2027 sales.

It has been revealed that that's not completely unreasonable for a biotech of this size with a transformative upcoming treatment that could become the standard of care across several oncology indications, the largest market in the pharmaceutical industry. Of course, there is some uncertainty to consider. Revolution Medicines might not make as much next year as some analysts expect.

There is also the possibility of clinical and regulatory setbacks. Even so, Rasonque's trajectory so far, and the fact that clinical progress has been strong -- and Revolution Medicines has a robust pipeline -- make a strong case for the stock. That's especially true since Rasonque recently earned approval in Europe.

And Revolution Medicines will also seek approvals in other countries, including Japan. In my view, the opportunity in the U.S. alone, where Revolution Medicines estimates that about 55,000 new cases of metastatic pancreatic cancer occur annually, justifies its current valuation. So, the stock is worth buying right now and holding onto for at least the next five years.

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that privacy concerns around AI agents have prompted encrypted messaging app Signal to set new limits on screenshots.
  • According to recent reports, whittaker noted that Google and Apple’s agentic features, including Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI’s Onscreen Awareness, compromise the privacy missions of third-party developers.
  • Also: My 5 favorite Siri AI ‘onscreen awareness’ tricks – and why.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that privacy concerns around AI agents have prompted encrypted messaging app Signal to set new limits on screenshots. The firm will prevent screenshotting in its iOS 27 app and “when AI assistants attempt to capture screen data on Android,” Signal President Meredith Whittaker wrote in a blog post Friday.

According to recent reports, whittaker noted that Google and Apple’s agentic features, including Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI’s Onscreen Awareness, compromise the privacy missions of third-party developers. These features observe what’s on a user’s screen as context for completing requests.

Also: My 5 favorite Siri AI ‘onscreen awareness’ tricks – and why.

Industry observers note that “Your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” Whittaker said. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.”.

Signal also blocked screenshots last year in response to Microsoft’s controversial Recall AI feature, which could capture screenshots of Signal chats on devices running Windows 11.

Recent findings suggest that signal’s move is another reminder of how Significant Tech’s AI strategy trickles downstream. As AI features have moved from services external to the OS (like chatbots from OpenAI or Anthropic) to further inside of it, third-party apps have to adapt to conditions that undermine their hard-won privacy infrastructure.

Also: How I use Meta Muse safely to stretch my AI budget – and what I never let it do.

Industry observers note that just last week, researchers at Google DeepMind used AI agents to formally verify Signal’s code, building on Signal’s own work to essentially prove the app’s encryption works. That’s a high bar for a security guarantee within the app, but it becomes meaningless if an agent can simply grab messages off a screen.

Samsung is reportedly working on its own agent, Galaxy Claw, and Apple is developing a rival for Claude and ChatGPT as well.

Whittaker noted Signal’s screenshot restriction isn’t perfect, saying that AI agents can still access app data through other means, “such as retrieving content already present on a user’s device via the filesystem.” Earlier this week, a Reuters investigation supported by Signal and the AI Now Institute found that Meta’s Muse AI agent was using permissions from its initial setup in unexpected ways to access apps and data that a user had not explicitly connected it to.

Signal said its protections don’t at the moment work on MacOS.

According to recent reports, “It is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy,” she added. “Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience.”.

If you’d still like to take screenshots, you can simply disable the setting, though Signal’s announcement strongly advised against it.

“Doing so will potentially expose your (and your contacts’) Signal content to these AI agents, and break our privacy guarantees,” Whittaker said.

#16479. Why You Shouldn’t Use Meta’s Muse AI Agent for Shopping Next Weekend

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1013 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Why You Shouldn’t Use Meta’s Muse AI Agent for Shopping Next Weekend

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1013 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s been over two months since Meta debuted its Muse AI agent, giving people new tools to automate tasks like handling email replies, booking travel or even shopping for you.
  • Muse has been highly controversial, the subject of several security warnings and privacy breaches.
  • According to recent reports, AI agents are marketed as providing convenience by acting on your behalf.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s been over two months since Meta debuted its Muse AI agent, giving people new tools to automate tasks like handling email replies, booking travel or even shopping for you.

Muse has been highly controversial, the subject of several security warnings and privacy breaches. Meta’s Muse AI agent quietly builds a profile on you the second you start using it, even if you explicitly tell it not to. That turns Jolly, its supposedly cute and cuddly mascot, into the friendly face of some serious security flaws.

According to recent reports, AI agents are marketed as providing convenience by acting on your behalf. But the trade-off is privacy and control. You’re handing over your personal information to a black box with little visibility into how it’s used. Multiple incidents are fueling a conversation about the dangers of agentic AI and whether they require higher security standards before being granted access to user data.

According to recent reports, that’s especially the case when it comes to handing over sensitive financial information. If you give an AI access to your digital wallets to shop for you, the risk extends beyond an authorized purchase. You could be exposing your bank accounts to a potential security breach or data exposure, with little recourse to fix it. If you were considering letting Muse make decisions and transactions with your money ahead of Black Friday and Cyber Monday, you should know it’s still raising red flags as a shopping companion.

Given Meta’s track record of privacy fines, data sharing and security issues, it’s worth proceeding with caution. A few months ago, a lifestyle blogger reported that the social media platform’s AI asked intrusive questions about her kids and pieced together private information about her life from her posts. Meta’s controversial smart glasses have received pushback on multiple fronts — from its facial recognition software to the way it captures and stores data.

It has been revealed that despite the risk, Muse has remained popular and now faces competition from Anthropic’s newly released Claude Duet, another AI business agent. Meta is also releasing a $300 portable device, Charm, in a virtual-toy style that will work with Muse.

A representative for Meta has not responded to CNET’s request for comment.

According to recent reports, muse asks for the keys to your digital life: passwords, full disk access, emails, calendar invites, contacts, Notes and WhatsApp chats. Meta also feeds your conversations into its AI training pipeline by default, leaving it on you to dig through the settings and opt out.

Within weeks of launch earlier this fall, a security researcher demonstrated that the assistant could be hijacked via a zero-day exploit that Meta’s own documentation acknowledged was easy to trigger. Then, an investigative journalist discovered Muse digging through his private Apple Messages without permission. Meta disputed the claim, but Apple took it seriously enough to roll out an emergency revision to MacOS privacy controls.

More recently, Meta employees themselves have flagged instances where Muse may have accessed encrypted messages from apps such as Signal or information from other Muse customers, which Meta has chalked up to “isolated incidents” and that permission to access apps and information from notifications has to be explicitly granted in a statement to news outlets.

If the previous incidents weren’t enough to give you pause, there’s also a widely publicized case in which Muse mistakenly shared the home address of a Toronto tech reviewer, Matt Robb, with a potential buyer on Facebook Marketplace. Muse invited the stranger to Robb’s home without his explicit consent or knowledge, then later apologized for doing so, as detailed in a Threads post. Robb hadn’t realized that he had inadvertently granted Muse blanket permission to automatically reply to Marketplace inquiries using the details he provided, including his address.

Before facing a potential security nightmare, here are a few other things to know about Muse.

Muse uploads iOS or Mac data even when you tell it not to: Meta’s Muse appears to blatantly ignore user permissions, according to a September report by AppleInsider. In one case, the AI agent synced roughly 187,000 lines of a user’s Apple Messages without their consent, even though “Full Disk Access” was turned off. The report shows that Muse pinged a user’s messages database thousands of times despite disk access being disabled. Muse then successfully harvested texts from the user’s Mac — not from Meta’s Messenger, but from Apple Messages. Even people who refuse to use Muse may have their data collected by the AI if they text someone who does have it installed.

Industry observers note that muse could hand over data to human callers: Before Meta launched the ability for its Muse to make outbound business calls on your behalf, internal Meta documents revealed that the organization planned to rely on human contractors at call centers to help make reservations and appointments. That means not only would the software have access to all your private data, but a total stranger might also be managing your personal commitments — all without your knowledge. The human concierge feature appears to have been rolled back for now, according to Reuters.

It has been revealed that muse has the most robust data collection: In September, the VPN company Surfshark noted it found that Meta Muse is collecting — or attempting to collect — 31 out of 35 types of data, putting it far ahead of other popular chatbots like Gemini, ChatGPT and DeepSeek. Muse also collects highly sensitive personal information like location data, sexual orientation, genetic information or biometric data. Muse (along with Meta AI and Gemini) also reserves the right to use collected audio data for other purposes, such as analytics or product personalization. Surfshark released a full dataset of what it uncovered.

Meta has tried hard with Muse to make the AI agent seem cute and approachable, but when it comes to your money and giving Muse access to it, it’s best to be very cautious for the time being.

Atmos Rewards is the airline loyalty program for Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines. One of its newer features is Atmos Communities, which offer additional rewards and benefits tailored to different travel interests.

It has been revealed that there are six communities, including two reserved for Alaska and Hawaii residents. The other four are open to members regardless of where they live. But don’t get caught up in the community names. The best choice for you may depend more on your travel plans than the groupings suggest.

Here’s how to decide which Atmos Community best fits your travel patterns.

» Learn more: The guide to Atmos Rewards.

Atmos Communities are like groups within the Atmos Rewards program that offer additional benefits based on different travel interests.

They’re free to join for Atmos Rewards members. Four communities are available to all members, while community Club 49 is reserved for Alaska residents and community Huaka’i by Hawaiian is reserved for Hawaii residents.

In a recent development, you can belong to only one community at a time and switch communities once per calendar year. Consider your upcoming travel plans before choosing.

Recent findings suggest that each Atmos Community has a list of 10 destinations where members can earn bonus points and status points. Although the destinations differ by community, the rewards structure is the same.

Industry observers note that through Dec. 31, 2027, members can earn up to 10,000 bonus points and 10,000 status points by visiting qualifying destinations.

Here’s how many points you’ll earn as you reach each milestone:.

Visit one destination, earn 100 status and bonus points.

Visit two destinations, earn 200 status and bonus points.

Visit three destinations, earn 300 status and bonus points.

Visit four destinations, earn 400 status and bonus points.

Visit five destinations, earn 500 status and bonus points.

Visit six destinations, earn 750 status and bonus points.

Visit seven destinations, earn 1,000 status and bonus points.

Visit eight destinations, earn 1,250 status and bonus points.

Visit nine destinations, earn 2,500 status and bonus points.

Visit 10 destinations, earn 3,000 status and bonus points.

The first member of each community to visit all 10 qualifying destinations during the challenge period will also earn 100,000 bonus points.

Latest lists of qualifying destinations for each community take effect on Jan. 1, 2028.

Here’s a closer look at the six communities, their benefits and the destinations eligible for bonus points.

Global Locals is geared toward frequent international travelers. Benefits include:.

Earn 10% more status points toward Atmos elite status on flights that begin and/or end outside the U.S., including award flights.

Earn 1 status point for every 25 points transferred to Atmos Rewards from Bilt or Marriott Bonvoy.

Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

Industry observers note that through Dec. 31, 2027, these 10 Oneworld Alliance hubs count toward bonus points and status points. Qualifying layovers also count toward the destination challenge, so you don’t necessarily need to make these cities your final stop.

If you frequently travel internationally or have any upcoming flights through any of these airports, including qualifying layovers, Global Locals might be a fit for you.

If you have the Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® credit card, you’ll earn 3 Atmos points per $1 spent on eligible Alaska and Hawaiian Airlines purchases, dining and foreign transactions. The last bonus category can be especially useful for frequent international travelers.

This community has a similar setup to Global Locals, but most of its bonus destinations are in the U.S. Here’s what you can get:.

Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

Families On the Go might appeal to you if you redeem Atmos Rewards for your children. Benefits include:.

Get 20% of your points back on eligible award flights for kids 12 and under after you complete your trip.

Exclusively for Alaska residents, Club 49 offers rewards that are focused on travel to, from and within the state:.

Two free checked bags when traveling to or from Alaska on Alaska Airlines or Hawaiian Airlines.

Three free checked bags when traveling within Alaska on Alaska Airlines.

While this community is only for Alaskans, you might decide one of the other communities more closely matches your travel plans — especially if you already have an Alaska credit card with free baggage benefits. However, if you ship a lot of cargo or think you’ll use the Travel Now discounts, those are special benefits that may sway you to choose Club 49.

Hawaii residents have their own community just for them: Huaka’i by Hawaiian. It offers benefits focused on interisland travel:.

Two free checked bags on neighbor island flights on Hawaiian Airlines, including sports equipment like surfboards and golf bags.

Quarterly fare discounts of 10% off one neighbor island booking, or 20% off for eligible Hawaiian Airlines® World Elite Mastercard® and Atmos™ Rewards Visa® cardholders.

Don’t be persuaded by the names of the communities. Look a little deeper, because there’s a lot of overlap between destination lists. Compare the options against your upcoming travel plans.

According to recent reports, you can change communities once per calendar year, so you aren’t locked in to your initial choice indefinitely. However, switching communities resets your destination-challenge progress, but you’ll retain any points you’ve already earned.

Sources indicate that if your home airport (or one you visit frequently) is already on a community’s list, you may have an easier time earning points. Also consider whether a particular community benefit, such as free checked bags or points back on award flights for kids, outweighs the destination challenge.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google Home is replacing Nest and bringing latest devices.
  • If you’re a Nest smart home user, a major change is coming in early 2027 that will affect how you manage your smart home.
  • Recent findings suggest that all Nest devices will lose Nest app support in favor of the Google Home app, and the Nest app will be retired on Jan.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google Home is replacing Nest and bringing latest devices.

If you’re a Nest smart home user, a major change is coming in early 2027 that will affect how you manage your smart home. Google has officially confirmed to CNET via email that both the Nest app and Google Assistant are being sunset, and current customers will lose access to both next year.

Recent findings suggest that all Nest devices will lose Nest app support in favor of the Google Home app, and the Nest app will be retired on Jan. 25, 2027. Google Assistant will be removed from home devices on Aug. 2, 2027, with all support moving to the Gemini for Home voice assistant.

In a recent development, the change is part of Google’s effort to consolidate its various apps and devices into a single app and voice experience. In a statement sent to CNET, Google confirmed that “every device supported today works with these updated experiences.”.

Nest Thermostats should all seamlessly port over to Google Home.

Google has confirmed that Google Home will support all your Nest devices, including thermostats, cameras, doorbells, smoke detectors and locks. Existing schedules and settings should transfer over automatically, which is often a hassle when you switch between apps and devices. You should also be able to pair your Nest devices with any Works with Google Home and Matter smart home devices, as well as Google Home speakers and smart displays and TV streamers, all with the same app.

It has been revealed that as part of the switchover, you should be able to access Nest devices on various platforms outside of the mobile app. It’ll support iOS and Android widgets, the Home Panel on Android, smart displays, speakers and the Google Home web page. That includes being able to check live camera views, adjust your thermostat and lock your front door, right from a TV or smartwatch.

Google Assistant may be leaving, but Google is releasing newer, more powerful devices.

According to recent reports, google indicates that, in addition to devices automatically appearing in the Favorites tab in the Google Home app, you should be able to see camera views faster and access the most-used controls the moment you open the app. Part of the goal is to give owners the latest security protections and cyber defenses, as well as Google Account security, privacy controls and threat protections –- all things that seem extra relevant these days as major companies across the US seem to be experiencing outages.

However, to continue controlling and receiving notifications from your Nest devices remotely, you will need to switch to the Google Home app or home.google.com if you prefer to control them via a web browser.

You can change Google voice assistant voices, but not the wake words.

On Aug. 2, 2027, Gemini for Home voice assistant will fully replace Google Assistant on speakers and smart displays. The switch to Gemini makes a lot of sense if you’ve used Google Assistant at all. Assistant is very much an older voice assistant, lacking the smarter follow-ups and natural-language capabilities that make Gemini more useful.With Gemini, you should get answers to more complex questions, and you can speak more naturally without barking commands, letting it handle conversation context and remember multiple interactions.

Getting ready for Google Home is easy, though Google has an entire Nest App Transition Support Hub if you need step-by-step instructions to walk you through everything that’s needed.

For most people, it should be a simple matter of downloading the Google Home app. Naturally, a Google Account is required, but as mentioned, your Nest devices, including the cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app starting on Jan. 25, 2027.

Gemini’s Google Home integrations are useful, but command options can include some risks.

Sources indicate that the other thing you may have to do is download any custom video clips you’ve created on home.nest.com. Manually saved clips won’t transfer to the Google Home app along with your video history. To make sure these are backed up, you’ll want to visit home.nest.com before Jan. 25, 2027, and use the Download All button to save clips you want to keep.

The final deadline to migrate your Nest account to a Google account before the manufacturer starts data deletions March 25, 2027.

Google indicates Nest devices, including cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app to the Google Home app. Nest Aware (1st Gen) subscriptions should also automatically switch to Google Home Premium so that coverage continues without interruption. Google Home Premium is replacing Nest Aware (1st Gen), and owners will receive an email closer to the transfer date detailing your subscription information.

Google’s smart displays should all work perfectly with the various Nest devices.

Gemini for Home is already available in many countries and languages. Google unveiled earlier that it’s expanding to more regions over the coming months. Customers in a supported region can upgrade to Gemini Home right now.

According to recent reports, on your phone, open the latest version of the Google Home app, tap your profile icon in the top right to open Home Settings, then tap “Get Started” on the “Set up Gemini for Home” banner. On your computer, just visit home.google.com/gemini.

Mortgage rates dropped today, but anything above 7% still puts pressure on home buyers’ budgets.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.24% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points lower than yesterday and three basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

According to recent reports, A significant drop is eye-catching, but you should consider mortgage interest rates' overall direction, not just what's going on today. While the economy never sleeps, markets are closed on the weekends. The rates you see Friday are unlikely to change much (if at all) until Monday.

Recent findings suggest that mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to newly introduced inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Next week, the Nerds are waiting for the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a massive reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

It has been revealed that if PCE indicates inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes. (An increase to the federal funds rate is already widely expected at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.) A cooler reading could ease some pressure on mortgage rates for now.

I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though. Last week's Producer Price Index showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its fastest pace in four years. Wholesale inflation measures the price businesses pay for things. When businesses’ costs go up, they could pass those along to consumers in the form of higher prices — keeping the flames of inflation alive.

Whether Wednesday's PCE brings relief or another helping of bad inflation news, we'll know before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.74% or higher.

Sources indicate that also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a latest home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.
