10 stocks we like better than Take-Two Interactive Software ›.

Industry observers note that the reviews are in for Grand Theft Auto VI, and they are glowing. The reviewer for the gaming publication IGN called it "the single most impressive video game I have ever played.".

Gamespot's review called it "an astonishing open-world action game that I'd wager won't be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7.".

Metacritic gave it a score of 99 out of 100 based on 151 critic reviews -- the site's highest score ever.

Wall Street is also blown away by the revenue-generating potential of GTA VI and is bullish on Take-Two Interactive (TTWO +0.65%), the organization that produces GTA VI. Of the 31 analysts who cover Take-Two stock, 97% rate it as a buy with a median price target of $290 per share, implying 39% upside from its current price.

According to the tech giant, GTA VI sold 32.5 million copies of the game during the pre-sale period, a record. And including pre-sales and sales on the first day it was available to buy on Nov. 19, the game generated $3.79 billion in sales.

That is a one-day record for the entertainment industry across any medium, the firm remarked. This was significanly higher than the projected pre-sale totals and the one-day net revenue projections by industry trackers. The sales numbers already cover the gameʻs production and marketing costs, estimated at $1 billion to $1.5 billion.

According to recent reports, take-Two Interactive expects between $8 billion and $8.2 billion in net bookings this fiscal year ending March 31, 2027. Net bookings refer to revenue from both games sold and in-game purchases. That would be about 21% higher, at the midpoint, than the $6.7 billion in net bookings it saw last fiscal year.

But one Wall Street analyst sees Take-Two blowing past that estimate.

This week, analysts at Wells Fargo (WFC -2.47%) updated their sales projections for Take-Two in light of the pre-sales and sales trends for GTA VI.

In a recent development, wells Fargo anticipates that GTA VI will sell 65 million copies by the end of Take-Two's fiscal 2027 on March 31. Based on its forecasts, Wells Fargo projects net bookings this fiscal year to be $9.76 billion. That's 19% higher than previous estimates and some $1.6 billion, or 20%, more than Take-Two's own guidance at the midpoint.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Sources indicate that the estimate anticipates a significant boost coming from the release of the PC and online versions of GTA VI in early 2027. Currently, only the single-player version of the game has been released. The online version is the multiplayer game. According to reports, GTA V, which came out in 2013, still generates about $500 million per year from the multiplayer game, so it goes without saying that GTA VI online will be a massive sales boost.

Recent findings suggest that analysts at Wedbush estimate sales of 30 million to 40 million copies by the end of calendar 2026. That would beat the roughly 29 million copies GTA V sold in the first month after its release in 2013. GTA V went on to sell some 235 million copies, making it the second best-selling game of all time.

In a recent development, in its guidance, Take-Two calls for net bookings of $3.35 billion to $3.5 billion in its fiscal 2027 Q3, which ends Dec. 31, and revenue of $3.27 billion to $3.42 billion. That would be up from net bookings of $1.76 billion and revenue of $1.7 billion in fiscal 2026 Q3.

It has been revealed that that's why investors should expect GTA VI to provide a strong multiyear boost to revenue and earnings. It's a game that takes 100 or more hours to complete, doing all the side quests, so it will engage players for a long time and prompt in-game purchases. Plus, when the multiplayer game comes out next year, it will generate recurring revenue as players go through the game multiple times with friends and others, and make in-game purchases. The $500 million in annual revenue from GTA V is testament to that.

Take-Two stock had a 25% run-up the week before the Nov. 19 release to $230 per share and has since settled back down to around $208 per share in a sell-the-news scenario. But that just makes for a better entry price.

Take-Two stock is reasonably valued at 28 times forward earnings and is a solid buy right now. GTA VI should generate strong revenue and boost earnings not just this fiscal year, but in the years ahead, as GTA V did following its release in 2013. Over the last 10 years, Take-Two stock has posted an average annualized return of 16%.

College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1375 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college.
  • Industry observers note that before you go searching for a scholarship, it's vital to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
  • Scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

Industry observers note that before you go searching for a scholarship, it's vital to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

Scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

These scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

Some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s notable to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

In a recent development, merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

Sources indicate that merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

It has been revealed that merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

Recent findings suggest that some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that shows more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

Sources indicate that unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

Some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

Athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

Recent findings suggest that even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

Some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

Scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

Recent findings suggest that which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

Veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

Industry observers note that scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

The best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

Recent findings suggest that think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

Apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. Even small scholarships can make a big impact when you add several of them together.

Understand how you can use the money. If you already have a scholarship that covers only books, applying for the same type of scholarship isn’t helpful if you don’t need the extra funds. Instead, look for scholarships that cover the costs you have remaining.

Not sure where to look? Our sister site Scholarships360.org provides students with vetted scholarship opportunities. That would be a good place to start.

His choice to represent his nation was condemned by some reporters back on Merseyside, amid fears of aggravating the injury and compromising his involvement for his club over the coming weeks as the fixtures come thick and fast for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Rossi was defiant when quizzed about Szoboszlai ahead of Hungary’s match against Northern Ireland on Tuesday night.

Sources indicate that he told reporters (via Origo Sport): “Did you see any problems with Dominik in the Georgia game? Because I didn’t see any. He played like he usually does, so there are no problems from our side. He says he’s ready, he’s available, so he’ll play.”.

The Hungary boss was true to his word, as the Liverpool star played the entirety of the Northern Ireland game, thankfully seeming to come through it without any adverse effects.

10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

The torch in AI has been passed.

It seems fitting in some ways that Anthropic's (ANT -8.50%) IPO came just a week after Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, leaving the chipmaker in turmoil. Nvidia had been the stock market's avatar for AI since the launch of ChatGPT, but with Anthropic now becoming the first AI lab to go public, it's set to take over as the market's best reflection of AI sentiment.

Anthropic is a pure-play AI tech giant founded in 2021 by a group of former OpenAI employees who thought that company was too weak on safety. Anthropic builds AI models and software products based on its frontier intelligence platform, Claude.

Anthropic's IPO also gave the firm a chance to have the investing world's full attention, and CEO Dario Amodei spoke for about five minutes at the Nasdaq stock exchange Thursday, sharing his vision for the company. Here are three things investors should know about the newly public company, direct from Amodei.

It has been revealed that dario Amodei. Image source: Getty Images.

Anthropic has made its prioritization of safety clear from its inception, and AI safety has only become more salient amid concerns of AI models going rogue, escaping sandboxes, and the intensifying competition with China.

It has been revealed that anthropic's emphasis on safety may also be a competitive advantage at a time when AI is facing a backlash. The midterm elections reflected growing discontent with data centers and could lead to a slowdown or increased restrictions on them, at least in some states.

The emphasis on safety also acts in the manufacturer's interest in terms of liability and reputational damage, as the future of AI is wide open and will be determined by companies like Anthropic.

Amodei told the audience, "There's a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety, and an obsession with safety and public benefit has been built into Anthropic's DNA from the start.".

Amodei wants everyone, including investors, users, and AI skeptics, to know that he's one of the good guys.

In a similar vein, Amodei described a best-case scenario for the AI competition as a "race to the top.".

Amodei mentioned, "If we can show it's possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful organization, others will be inspired to do the same.".

If that spirit takes hold in the industry, then, he said, everybody wins, no matter who has the best models. Amodei assured investors that they intend to lead that race, saying, "The race to the top works best when driven from the front of the pack, and we fully hope and expect to do so, but the goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.".

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Amodei began his comments with a story about how his father died of a disease, Hepatitis C, that was cured just a few years later.

The event clearly showed Amodei the power of invention and new technology, and after beginning his career in biology, he moved over to artificial intelligence, where he sees the potential for tremendous breakthroughs in medicine and beyond.

The departure of Jensen Huang due to a scandal involving multiple affairs is a reminder of the importance of character in leadership, and Amodei seems to possess that sufficiently.

Anthropic is a mission-driven company and the rare public benefit corporation on the stock market. Amodei brings a deep commitment to that mission and a personal passion for research and intelligence that can cure diseases and solve humanity's most pressing problems.

That's good news for Anthropic investors and should reassure them at a time when the AI trade looks more wobbly than ever.

    #16466. How Often Do You Need To Scrub The Do Not Call List? The 31-Day Rule Explained

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1029 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    How Often Do You Need To Scrub The Do Not Call List? The 31-Day Rule Explained

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1029 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Phil Portman is a serial entrepreneur and the Founder & CEO of Textdrip — a small business SMS marketing tool to automate SMS campaigns.
    • ​I see businesses repeatedly making the same mistake: They scrub their contact list once and then keep calling and texting from that list for months.
    • After years of experience working in a regulated industry, I’m sure about one thing: Businesses rarely fail because the rules are unclear.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Phil Portman is a serial entrepreneur and the Founder & CEO of Textdrip — a small business SMS marketing tool to automate SMS campaigns.

    ​I see businesses repeatedly making the same mistake: They scrub their contact list once and then keep calling and texting from that list for months. That’s a risky habit, because every day fresh numbers join the Do Not Call Registry. A list that was clean in January can be full of problems by March.

    After years of experience working in a regulated industry, I’m sure about one thing: Businesses rarely fail because the rules are unclear. They fail because their processes break down in practice. The Do Not Call rules are a crystal-clear example of this.

    Industry observers note that how often do you have to scrub the Do Not Call (DNC) list? Every 31 days. To keep safe harbor protection, you need to scrub against a version of the registry that is no more than 31 days old. In practice, that means every month.

    Recent findings suggest that the National Do Not Call Registry is run by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC). It lets people add their personal phone numbers to a list that tells telemarketers to stop contacting them. It exists to protect consumers who don’t want sales calls. It covers personal numbers, such as home and mobile lines. It doesn’t cover business-to-business calls to a organization line. Knowing this difference helps you decide which numbers need a check.

    Many teams assume it only covers voice calls, but it doesn’t. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) treats text messages as calls, so the same protections apply to SMS marketing. If you text prospects, those numbers also need a DNC check.

    State lists exist as well. Some states keep their own Do Not Call lists, and some, such as Florida and Texas, have stricter rules than the federal registry. If you contact people in several states, you need to check each state’s rules before you launch.

    Some calls are exempt, such as those to people who gave written permission or have an established business relationship with you. Even then, you must honor opt-out requests.

    Recent findings suggest that to qualify for safe harbor under FTC and FCC regulations, telemarketers must scrub their list against the National DNC Registry. Every call must be made using a registry version downloaded no more than 31 days earlier. Simply put, you must rescrub every month. If it’s day 32, you’re already at risk.

    Suppose you scrubbed a list on the first of the month. On the 20th, a prospect joins the registry. Your team keeps working that same list. Any call made after day 31 relies on an outdated version. Many teams scrub only when they upload new leads. This sounds fine, but a campaign can run for weeks, and a number can join the registry halfway through. If you keep contacting that number, you’re working from outdated data.

    Industry observers note that safe harbor is a defense that protects a business when a call goes out by mistake. But it only applies if you had a working process in place before the mistake happened. A written policy that nobody reads or follows won’t help. Training without a current list won’t help either.

    The FCC rule lists what a DNC safe harbor process needs:.

    • Written Do Not Call procedures.

    • Staff trained on those procedures.

    • An internal Do Not Call list that is kept up to date.

    • Registry access used to scrub within the 31-day window.

    • Logs (records) showing when each scrub happened.

    Record-keeping is a common gap. Without records, you have no safe harbor, even if the scrub did happen. If a regulator or a lawyer asks for proof, saying “we did it” won’t be enough. You need proof (dates and logs).

    Industry observers note that do Not Call violations get expensive promptly. Under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA), a consumer can sue for $500 per violation. If the violation was willful or knowing, a court can raise that to $1,500 per violation. A consumer generally must receive more than one call from the same business within 12 months to bring a DNC claim.

    In a recent development, some of these claims are filed as class actions. One outdated list can hold thousands of people, and each one may have a claim. A small gap in your process can turn into a very large bill. Legal fees and settlements add to that, along with damage to your business reputation.

    In a recent development, I lead a manufacturer in a regulated industry, so I think about this often. Compliance works best when it is practiced as a routine instead of an event. We built Landline Remover to help teams make scrubbing a routine.

    Industry observers note that 1. Scrub every time you upload leads, not just on launch day.

    Sources indicate that 2. Rescrub active lists monthly, ideally a few days before the 31-day window closes.

    In a recent development, 3. Check your internal list and the national list together. Your internal do-not-call list holds people who told you directly to stop. The registry doesn’t know about them. Both lists matter.

    4. Check reassigned numbers. Numbers change owners. The FCC’s reassigned numbers database can tell you whether a number has changed hands since you got consent.

    It has been revealed that 5. Log every scrub with the date. That log is your proof if a court or regulator asks.

    In a recent development, 6. Automate the scrubbing process so it doesn’t depend on memory.

    Do Not Call compliance is a monthly habit, not a one-time task. The rule is simple: scrub within 31 days, every time.

    It has been revealed that DNC scrubbing alone can’t protect a business. You need to keep proof that you followed the rule. Scrubbing only protects you if you can prove it. So build a regular scrubbing habit and keep the records. Remember that regulators don’t just look at your efforts—they ask for evidence.

    Breaking: Your Employees’ Personal AI Agents Are Becoming Your Security Problem

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1012 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • David Goldschlag is co-founder and CEO of Aembit, an identity control plane for AI agents.
    • ​Ahead of an important client meeting, a sales representative connects their personal AI agent to firm email and files.
    • Personal AI agents, including Meta’s Muse, OpenAI’s Dots and Google’s Gemini Spark, are software assistants that can carry out routine tasks across connected services and continue working between conversations.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    David Goldschlag is co-founder and CEO of Aembit, an identity control plane for AI agents.

    ​Ahead of an important client meeting, a sales representative connects their personal AI agent to firm email and files. The setup takes minutes and allows the employee to arrive prepared with considerably less effort, but that well-meaning shortcut may carry risks the rep never considered.

    Personal AI agents, including Meta’s Muse, OpenAI’s Dots and Google’s Gemini Spark, are software assistants that can carry out routine tasks across connected services and continue working between conversations. It is early, and there is little data yet on how often employees connect these personal assistants to manufacturer accounts. But if the first numbers are any indication, the habit is forming quickly. Meta noted Muse passed 10 million accounts within roughly six weeks of launch, and a Menlo Ventures survey found that 32% of U.S. adults who use AI have already let it act on their behalf without final sign-off.

    For security leaders who remember the first requests to connect personal smartphones to tech giant email, the arrival of these agentic deputies has a familiar feel. Employees found something useful and expected to use it, while IT and security were left to reconcile that enthusiasm with responsibility for company data.

    According to recent reports, bring-your-own-device (BYOD) policies and years of “shadow IT” disputes established an enduring reality: The rank and file would have a say in the technology they used. But the analogy has limits in the AI era. Traditional software generally follows predefined workflows, while an agent can choose which tools to use and which steps to take in carrying out an employee’s request, without the employee directing each action.

    Permissions granted with little consideration during setup can later support a series of actions the employee never specifically contemplated. For CISOs, the difficulty is deciding how much authority should accompany that discretion and how to enforce those limits once an AI assistant begins working.

    It has been revealed that consider the employee preparing for the customer meeting. The request of their agent sounds innocuous: Review recent correspondence, find the relevant account documents and prepare a briefing.

    Yet the permissions available during setup may cover far more information than this assignment requires. Depending on the connection, the agent may receive access to a mailbox containing correspondence with hundreds of customers, along with internal discussions unrelated to the meeting.

    Suppose the employee also asks the agent to prepare and send an external follow-up. An internal document contains useful background, including an unannounced pricing change. The agent could incorporate that information into a customer message because it appears relevant to the assignment. Every connection involved might be permitted, even though the resulting disclosure was never intended. Read-only access offers limited reassurance if the agent can send what it reads through another service.

    Requiring employee approval before an agent receives access provides another safeguard, but its value depends on what the employee can reasonably assess. A consent screen can describe the permissions being requested without making clear how an agent could use them together. The employee may approve those permissions without anticipating the disclosure described above.

    Sources indicate that manufacturer policy must establish which resources an assistant may access and which actions require further review. Employees should understand their responsibilities, but connecting an agent should not leave them to determine how much authority the company is willing to delegate.

    The following practices can help security leaders establish those boundaries while giving employees a practical way to use personal AI agents.

    Verify that records identify which agent acted and whose authority it used. Logs that name only the employee may leave investigators unable to distinguish direct actions from those taken by an agent.

    Sources indicate that establish which accounts and resources it can access, whether it can act in the background and how the provider handles credentials and retrieved data. Approval of an assistant should not imply approval of every connection it supports.

    Where controls permit, restrict access to relevant resources and separate retrieval permissions from permission to publish or send. Enforce those limits at runtime, when the agent requests access. If a service offers only broad access, weigh that limitation in the approval decision.

    In a recent development, reserve employees’ attention for consequential decisions. Before an external message is sent, for example, let them review its recipients, attachments and exact content, with another review required if material details change.

    Ensure security can revoke an agent’s access without disabling the employee’s account. This gives security teams a way to intervene when an agent needs to be stopped. Here, that means access revocation: withdrawing the agent’s ability to use connected systems. Cutting off access, however, does not necessarily terminate the agent’s process.

    Test it against background activity and previously issued credentials, and measure how long it takes for subsequent requests to fail. Depending on the implementation, previously issued access tokens may remain usable until they expire, or a revocation decision may take time to reach every system involved. Incident procedures should account for the behavior observed in testing, including any additional steps required to contain ongoing activity.​​​.

    These practices also expose limitations that a policy document alone cannot resolve. If a provider cannot support sufficiently narrow access or useful audit records, the company may need to restrict the information available to that agent or decline the connection.​.

    Recent findings suggest that the BYOD experience offers a useful lesson about AI adoption. Employees’ preferences can influence company technology decisions long before a formal policy catches up. Security leaders should take seriously the reasons people want personal agents, including the convenience of using a tool they already know.

    A workable policy should give employees a clear route to request access, explain which uses are permitted and offer alternatives when a requested connection grants more authority than the business can accept. Security teams, in turn, need evidence that the agreed restrictions hold during actual use.​​​.

    Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.

    Sources indicate that the Bridgewater Associates founder said Bessent's strategy to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S. economy. Coupled with the Japanese government reducing its U.S. bond market exposure and surging long-dated American bond yields, Dalio said investors may want to prepare their portfolios for increased risk by owning cryptocurrencies and gold.

    "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Dalio noted that the Treasury Department has "only limited capacity" to buy back bonds. Bessent told CNBC on Thursday that his team was going to "make a market" and that the purchases would likely top $4 billion.

    The U.S. is spending about 40% more than it's bringing in, resulting in the burgeoning budget deficit, Dalio mentioned. The U.S. budget deficit topped $432 billion in July, but Bessent told CNBC that it's likely peaked under President Donald Trump's administration.

    Bessent said in the interview that a team was looking at ways to shrink spending by hundreds of billions of dollars. But Dalio said there is "very little ability" to do so given that it is either committed or considered essential.

    Sources indicate that after years of overspending, Dalio said total debt now dwarfs what the U.S. brings in each year. If the U.S. government was a business, Dalio said debt service payments would come in at roughly $11 trillion — about 200% of annual revenue.

    Dalio, 77, warned the cost of repaying principal and servicing the debt will only grow over time.

    Sources indicate that to solve this, Dalio noted the U.S. needs to carefully employ a three-part strategy to get the budget deficit down to 3% of gross domestic product.

    It has been revealed that first, Dalio mentioned the U.S. government needs to reduce its spending. Second, he said tax revenue needs to be raised. Finally, the Newly introduced York native and Harvard Business School alumni said lower interest rates were needed.

    Industry observers note that "All three need to happen concurrently so as to prevent any one from being too large," Dalio said. "If any one is too large, the adjustment will be traumatic.".

    Dalio cautioned against ramming through these adjustments by "force." For instance, "it would be very bad if the Federal Reserve unnaturally forced interest rates down," he said.

    According to recent reports, dalio mentioned it's notable to to take steps now, while the economy is healthy. An economy in recession requires increased government spending, he said.

    Industry observers note that dalio mentioned the exact timing of a debt crisis can be swayed by variables ranging from military conflict to political change. On its current trajectory, the U.S. could enter such a crisis in as early as one year or as late as five. "My guess, which I suppose will be a bad one, is that it will come in three years, give or take two, if the course we're on is not changed.".

    To prepare, Dalio recommended investors are underweight debt assets, such as bonds.

    As much as 10% to 15% of a portfolio could land in gold, as well as "a bit" of bitcoin, the hedge fund founder stated.

    It has been revealed that dalio's post came at the tail end of a volatile week for U.S. financial markets. Rising long-term Treasury yields have pressured stocks, leading the S&P 500 to snap a a three-week-long advance.

    #16461. The Next Software Revolution After AI Is Efficiency

    The Next Software Revolution After AI Is Efficiency

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1056 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Itamar Syn-Hershko, Founder of NeverBlink AI and BigData Boutique, helps companies confidently operate and optimize data platforms at scale.
    • For decades, we’ve made software easier to write, even when it meant making it more expensive to run.​.
    • Recent findings suggest that we introduced programming languages, frameworks and layers of abstraction that allowed developers to move faster.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Itamar Syn-Hershko, Founder of NeverBlink AI and BigData Boutique, helps companies confidently operate and optimize data platforms at scale.

    For decades, we’ve made software easier to write, even when it meant making it more expensive to run.​.

    Recent findings suggest that we introduced programming languages, frameworks and layers of abstraction that allowed developers to move faster. Along the way, we accepted higher memory consumption, more CPU usage and increasingly complex infrastructure.​.

    For the most part, this made sense. Developers were expensive, hardware kept getting cheaper and getting products to market rapidly was often more vital than squeezing the most out of every server.​.

    I think we’re approaching a point where that trade-off no longer makes sense.​.

    AI is changing the cost of writing software, while the growing demand for computing resources is making efficiency more key than it has been in years. Together, these forces could change not just how we build software but also the economics of the entire software industry.​.

    Sources indicate that take Java, for example. Much of its success came from making developers more productive. Automatic memory management, a rich ecosystem and portability made it easier to build and maintain complex applications without worrying about many of the details involved in lower-level programming.​.

    The trade-off was additional runtime overhead. Garbage collection, managed memory and abstraction layers can require considerably more resources than a carefully optimized native implementation.​.

    Industry observers note that this was often a perfectly reasonable compromise. If using Java saved months of engineering work, spending a little more on servers was easy to justify.​.

    But what happens when AI can write, maintain and optimize complex C++ or Rust code at a fraction of the previous engineering cost?​ We should start questioning whether some of the abstractions we’ve relied on for decades are still worth their price.​.

    I’m not suggesting we rewrite every Java application in assembly. There are good reasons to use managed languages, including their mature tooling, ecosystems and safety characteristics. AI-generated code also introduces its own risks and still needs careful review.​.

    But the argument that lower-level programming is too expensive or complicated to justify is becoming much weaker.​.

    ​At the same time, the infrastructure side of the equation is changing.​.

    Recent findings suggest that AI is creating enormous demand for computing capacity, memory, electricity and data center space. The International Energy Agency projects that global data center electricity consumption will roughly double by 2030.​.

    We cannot keep solving every software performance problem by adding more hardware. At some point, the availability and cost of that hardware become serious constraints.​.

    There’s also growing pressure to make software cheaper.​.

    AI is already reducing the time and effort involved in producing software, and we should expect some of those savings to reach customers. As it becomes cheaper to build competing products, companies will find it harder to justify high prices based on development costs alone.​.

    According to recent reports, this puts infrastructure efficiency at the center of the conversation. If two products offer comparable functionality but one requires a fraction of the hardware to operate, the difference can be substantial. The more efficient product can offer lower prices, better margins or both.​.

    ​Search engines and databases are good places to look for early examples.

    Recent findings suggest that ​Traditional search architectures (Lucene-based especially, such as Elasticsearch and OpenSearch) often require continuously provisioned compute resources and substantial memory to maintain indexes and deliver low-latency queries. This can make infrastructure costs difficult to align with fluctuating workloads.​.

    In a recent development, ​Companies such as turbopuffer and WarpSearch are challenging those assumptions. Both use an object-storage-first architecture for vector and full-text search, reducing the need to keep large indexes on expensive infrastructure. A Google Cloud case study reports search and storage cost reductions of 90% for its approach.

    ​There are examples outside search as well, including ClickHouse, Neon, Bun and more.

    ​These products aren’t necessarily the result of AI-assisted development. Many of their innovations started before today’s coding agents became widely available.

    ​What interests me is what happens when the engineering effort required to build systems like these drops dramatically.

    ​For engineering leaders, this should change how we evaluate technology choices.

    ​We spend a lot of time measuring developer productivity, feature delivery and time to market. We should be paying just as much attention to what our software costs to operate.

    Sources indicate that ​That starts with measuring actual resource consumption. Cost per query, cost per transaction, memory per workload and CPU utilization are not just infrastructure metrics. They directly affect the economics of the product.

    Recent findings suggest that ​It also means questioning architectural decisions we’ve come to accept. Does that service really need to run continuously? Does that dataset need to stay in memory? Are we using the right algorithms and data structures? Could a more efficient implementation eliminate entire servers?

    ​And perhaps most importantly, we should be using AI for more than producing code faster.

    ​AI can help investigate performance bottlenecks, evaluate alternative algorithms, rewrite expensive components and explore lower-level implementations that would previously have required too much engineering effort.

    Industry observers note that ​There are still trade-offs. Reliability, security, correctness and maintainability matter. An implementation that saves 20% in CPU costs but introduces serious operational risks is hardly an improvement.

    ​The point is that we now have more ways to pursue efficiency without paying the same development cost we once did.

    ​I expect we’ll see more companies challenge established software categories by building products that achieve similar results with much less infrastructure.

    Industry observers note that ​Some will use better algorithms. Others will rethink storage architectures, eliminate unnecessary compute or replace expensive runtime components. AI will make many of these approaches easier to implement.

    In a recent development, ​For established software vendors, this creates a real challenge. Their existing architectures may have been designed around assumptions that no longer hold, while newer competitors have the freedom to start from scratch.

    ​For customers, it should eventually mean more capable software at lower prices.

    ​We’ve spent decades making software easier and cheaper to write and accepting the infrastructure overhead that came with it.

    ​Now that writing software is becoming cheaper, it’s time to focus on making it cheaper to run.

    By Jonathan Ponciano – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:07PM EST.

    Nvidia's terrible month just got worse.

    In a recent development, shares of Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) fell 14% on Friday afternoon, to less than $126, after Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating the chipmaker's accounting. The drop erased roughly $491 billion in market value in a single session, taking Nvidia from about $3.52 trillion to about $3.03 trillion.

    According to recent reports, zoom out and the damage is even bigger. Nvidia closed at a record $239.24 on Oct. 6. At Friday's price, the stock is down about 48% from that high, and the firm has lost about $2.7 trillion in value in just six weeks.

    Here's what we know, and what investors should make of it.

    The Wall Street Journal first reported on Tuesday that the SEC was investigating Nvidia but couldn't say what the probe was about. On Friday, Reuters, citing two people briefed on the matter, reported that the agency's enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues at the firm.

    Sources indicate that many questions remain unanswered. Reuters couldn't determine when the inquiry began or which accounting practices are under review. The SEC declined to comment, and Nvidia didn't immediately respond. Keep in mind that the SEC investigates plenty of companies that are never charged with anything.

    The stock was already having a bad day before the report: shares were down more than 6% earlier in the session amid a broad sell-off in AI stocks.

    It has been revealed that the probe adds to a pile of problems. Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on Nov. 11 following revelations about his personal relationships, including with a woman U.S. authorities suspect of spying for China, which China denies. The Justice Department is also reviewing Nvidia's planned $12.9 billion purchase of Hugging Face, according to Reuters.

    Sources indicate that two areas could draw scrutiny. The first is how Nvidia reports where its sales come from. The company breaks out revenue by where customers are headquartered, rather than where they're billed. On that basis, about 63% of last quarter's revenue came from U.S.-based customers. The Financial Times has reported that Nvidia made the switch as sales billed to Singapore approached half of its total, a bad look with Southeast Asia having become a hub for chips smuggled into China.

    The second is how Nvidia helps its customers pay for its chips. On Tuesday's earnings call, interim CEO Colette Kress remarked Nvidia's guarantees totaled $118 billion at the end of the quarter, including $105 billion of credit support tied to a single data center campus. These guarantees are the kind of disclosure the SEC is watching closely at AI companies. When a chipmaker helps fund the projects that buy its chips, it's harder to tell how much demand would exist on its own.

    None of this has shown up in the numbers yet. Nvidia's revenue jumped 103% to $115.8 billion last quarter, and the tech giant expects about $130 billion this quarter. Management even raised its growth forecast for next fiscal year to about 75%. At about $126, the stock trades at roughly 12 times last quarter's adjusted earnings of $2.68 per share on an annualized basis, cheap for a company growing this fast.

    But cheap can get cheaper. Accounting questions hit at the heart of what investors pay for: trust in the numbers. Until Nvidia names a permanent CEO and the SEC's focus becomes clearer, the stock could stay volatile, even after a 48% drop.

    For long-term investors who already own Nvidia, there's no need to panic-sell on a report about an investigation. For anyone thinking of buying, it's smarter to wait for more clarity, or to build a position slowly, than to bet that the worst is over. There are plenty of other semiconductor stocks without a cloud of investigations hanging over them.

    • In a recent development, marvell Technology (MRVL -11.69%) will release results for its fiscal third quarter of 2027 (the period ended Oct.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:23PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Marvell Technology ›.

    In a recent development, marvell Technology (MRVL -11.69%) will release results for its fiscal third quarter of 2027 (the period ended Oct. 31, 2026) on Tuesday, Dec. 1, with a conference call at 1:30 p.m. Pacific time.

    According to recent reports, the chipmaker's stock comes into the report at around $138 as I write, off about 56% from its June 4 record close of $316.43. And most of that drop is recent. Marvell shares ended Oct. 28 at around $252, the last trading day before speculation started about a deal for optical parts maker Lumentum Holdings.

    On Nov. 2, the two companies unveiled an all-stock deal. After it closes, Marvell's current shareholders will own around two-thirds of the combined manufacturer. The growth stock is down about 45% from that Oct. 28 close.

    It has been revealed that the Dec. 1 report will be Marvell's first full quarterly update since it agreed to buy Lumentum. And if the past three years are any guide, the shares might make a substantial move the day after.

    Recent findings suggest that matt Murphy. Image source: Getty Images.

    It has been revealed that marvell reports after the market closes, so the reaction shows up in the next day's trading. Here are its last 12 reports, the stock's close-to-close move the next day, and the revenue growth management guided for the following quarter over the quarter just reported.

    It has been revealed that data source: Yahoo Finance and Marvell. Calculations by author.

    Shares dropped the next day seven times and climbed five times.

    And the moves were massive either way. The average swing was around 12%, and seven of the 12 moves topped 10%.

    Sources indicate that interestingly, the quarters themselves were almost never to blame. In all 12 reports, Marvell's revenue came in above the midpoint of its guidance.

    It has been revealed that I think the outlook mattered more. In the six reports in which management guided to next-quarter revenue growth of 6% or lower (with one guide for a decline), the stock fell the next day five times, with an average drop of around 9%.

    In the six where it guided for about 8% or more, shares climbed four times, with an average gain of about 6%.

    Recent findings suggest that but six reports on either side doesn't prove much, and the pattern has a clear exception. In August 2026, management guided to third-quarter revenue of $3.15 billion, up 15% from the second quarter's $2.74 billion, the second-largest increase in the table. The stock still dropped 10% the next day.

    A possible reason is that expectations had risen with the tech firm's share price, which had more than tripled since the March 2026 report.

    This time, the quarter itself could hold even less surprise than normal. When it confirmed the Lumentum deal on Nov. 2, Marvell remarked preliminary third-quarter revenue was in line with its guidance. It kept the $3.15 billion midpoint and tightened the range to plus or minus 2%.

    Sources indicate that that puts the focus on the fiscal fourth quarter, and the bar is high for a chipmaker helped by demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. Marvell's revenue climbed 22% year over year in the final quarter of fiscal 2026. Growth then rose to 28% and 37% in the first two quarters of fiscal 2027. And the $3.15 billion third-quarter midpoint means growth of around 52%, an acceleration for a third straight quarter.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    "[W]e expect our revenue growth to accelerate further through the remainder of fiscal 2027," Marvell CEO Matt Murphy said in the firm's fiscal second-quarter earnings release.

    According to recent reports, for growth to keep accelerating in the fiscal fourth quarter, revenue would have to exceed $3.4 billion, or about 7% above the third-quarter midpoint. In other words, a guide that just keeps pace with the third quarter might land right around the line that has split the stock's past reactions.

    In the end, I'd expect a big move on Dec. 2 either way, and a down day has been a bit more common than an up day. But I wouldn't read much into one day's move when the Lumentum deal isn't expected to close until the first half of 2028.

    In a recent development, personally, I'd pay more attention to the size of the fourth-quarter guide than to the stock's reaction to it. Shares trade at around 20 times the earnings analysts expect for fiscal 2028, a price that seems reasonable if growth continues to accelerate. And if shares drop again on a guide that still demonstrates accelerating growth, I think the lower price might be worth considering for investors who can ride out more swings like these.

    What Security Teams Still Get Wrong About Asset Visibility

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1018 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Yochai Corem is GM of Exposure Management at Check Point Software.
    • Organizations have more asset data than ever, but turning that data into a reliable view of what they own, operate and expose remains difficult.
    • In a recent development, A server appears in three tools with different identifiers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Yochai Corem is GM of Exposure Management at Check Point Software.

    Organizations have more asset data than ever, but turning that data into a reliable view of what they own, operate and expose remains difficult.

    In a recent development, A server appears in three tools with different identifiers. A cloud workload has an owner who has left the business. A forgotten website remains online after the campaign that funded it has ended. Each leaves security teams with information they still have to investigate before they can act.

    Security leaders should judge asset visibility by how reliably it supports a decision. A useful inventory helps teams establish what an asset does, who is responsible for it, how it is protected and what should happen when a problem appears.

    Several familiar assumptions prevent organizations from reaching that standard.

    An incomplete configuration management database (CMDB) should prompt a review of how records are created, updated and retired.

    Start by defining its purpose. The CMDB should record the systems, services and dependencies needed to manage business operations, with accountable owners and lifecycle status. Detailed security telemetry can remain in specialist systems, linked through reliable identifiers. An impersonating website belongs in an external threat register connected to the affected brand.

    According to recent reports, then identify which sources can reveal missing records. Cloud platforms, endpoint management, identity providers, vulnerability scanners and procurement systems can each expose inconsistencies. Buying a service should trigger registration; retiring it should trigger checks that access, infrastructure and records have been removed.

    Reconciliation should reflect the pace of change. I would set a daily reconciliation target for cloud and endpoint feeds; use deployment and retirement events to trigger updates; and review unresolved discrepancies weekly. Quarterly ownership reviews can supplement those checks.

    An asset without an owner needs an interim accountable team and an escalation deadline. “Unknown” should describe an investigation in progress.

    The modern attack surface spans internal infrastructure, cloud workloads, software as a service (SaaS), internet-facing systems, supplier connections and the organization’s broader digital presence.

    Those categories need different forms of accountability. Infrastructure teams may manage servers, cloud teams manage workloads and business application owners sponsor SaaS services. Marketing or regional teams may control domains and social accounts. Supplier relationships require a business sponsor alongside technical oversight.

    In a recent development, security should establish a review and response process across those boundaries. A newly discovered domain needs ownership verification and an assessment of what it hosts. An unfamiliar SaaS service needs checks on its people, data and access. A fraudulent social account needs investigation and a disruption process.

    According to recent reports, review frequency should follow exposure and change, with continuous discovery where practical and scheduled reviews for ownership, supplier access and dormant services. This broader scope aligns with the National Institute of Standards and Technology’s (NIST) inclusion of hardware, software, services and supplier services in asset management.

    Leaders can test this assumption by following a newly discovered asset through the security process.

    Does discovery trigger checks for required endpoint protection, vulnerability scanning and an accountable owner? Does an unmanaged internet-facing system reach someone authorized to restrict or remove it? Can the organization confirm that the resulting action occurred?

    It has been revealed that these outcomes show whether visibility operates as a security control. The Center for Internet Security’s (CIS) Control 1 connects inventory management with identifying and addressing unauthorized or unmanaged assets.

    Industry observers note that useful measures include the time taken to assign ownership, the proportion of applicable assets covered by required controls and the age of unresolved discrepancies. A growing inventory count provides little reassurance when newly discovered systems remain unmanaged.

    Additional tools introduce additional records, each with its own identifiers, timestamps and assumptions.

    Effective reconciliation requires explicit rules. Stable cloud resource identifiers or device identifiers should take precedence over an Internet Protocol (IP) address that may change or be reused. Records need source and freshness information so teams can distinguish a current observation from a stale entry.

    According to recent reports, organizations also need rules for conflicting fields. The identity system may establish who uses a device, while a service registry identifies the team accountable for the application it supports. Those relationships should remain distinguishable.

    Cyber asset attack surface management (CAASM) can support this work. Organizations can also improve CMDB integrations, use cloud asset inventories and service catalogs, or build reconciliation workflows in their existing data platforms. The operational requirements remain consistent: reliable matching, clear authority for each field and a process for resolving exceptions.

    Discovery should initiate a decision about management, protection or retirement.

    A forgotten website needs an owner to confirm whether it still serves a business purpose. A vulnerable application needs assessment of its exposure, dependencies and operational constraints before a response is selected.

    In a recent development, that decision should remain traceable through completion. If a service is retired, verify that it is no longer reachable. If a security control is applied, confirm that it covers the intended asset. Updating the inventory should accompany the operational change.

    This ongoing connection between asset information and action also underpins continuous threat exposure management (CTEM).

    CTEM depends on this discipline throughout scoping, discovery, prioritization, validation and mobilization.

    In a recent development, an unknown asset cannot enter the prioritization process. A known asset without business context is difficult to rank. Missing dependencies weaken assessments of attack paths and change impact. An unknown owner delays action, while stale records undermine confirmation that an exposure has been reduced.

    CAASM and external attack surface management (EASM) can support these stages by reconciling internal records and discovering internet-facing assets. Their value depends on the ownership, decision rules and response processes surrounding them.

    In a recent development, security leaders should expect asset visibility to connect discovery with accountable action. Every significant asset needs enough current context for someone to determine its protection requirements, address its exposures and verify the result. That is how a reliable inventory helps reduce the opportunities available to an attacker.​.

    The 'debasement trade' returns after Bessent bond maneuver. Crypto and gold are back in style

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The debasement trade is gaining latest traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.
    • Industry observers note that the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S.
    • "The size of the Treasury purchases announced so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," stated Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The debasement trade is gaining latest traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

    Industry observers note that the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

    "The size of the Treasury purchases announced so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," stated Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

    Gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

    It has been revealed that bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

    Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

    Industry observers note that the U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

    The Treasury Department stated last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the intends.

    Recent findings suggest that last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "massive toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

    Long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

    In a recent development, "Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold noted in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

    The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

    The stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah said. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

    The Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah mentioned. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

    "The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah stated in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

    Coltman at 21Shares stated the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

    Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

    Sources indicate that deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh said in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

    Billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder said.

    "The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

    It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, stated Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

    #16448. Breaking: How To Teach Your AI Agent About Your Manufacturer

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (787 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: How To Teach Your AI Agent About Your Manufacturer

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (787 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Frederik Riskær Pedersen, Founder and CEO of Maplith, a organization brain for your AI agents.
    • According to recent reports, for 16 years, I ran a translation company that grew from a handful of people into an international business.
    • According to recent reports, one customer indicates it well.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Frederik Riskær Pedersen, Founder and CEO of Maplith, a organization brain for your AI agents.

    According to recent reports, for 16 years, I ran a translation company that grew from a handful of people into an international business. The most crucial thing I learned about knowledge is that it rarely lives where you think it does.

    According to recent reports, one customer indicates it well. We had to fetch their files from their own system and deliver them in their own layout, and we could only invoice some of the repetitions. None of that was written down anywhere. It lived with one project manager. Anyone else would have done it the standard way and got it wrong.

    That tailoring was not a side issue. It was the product. If the work had been standard, the customer could have run the model themselves. This is why a manufacturer’s rules never get standardized away: The exceptions are often exactly what customers pay for.

    I think of this every time someone asks me why their AI agent isn’t delivering. The models are good enough. The problem is that the agent starts from zero every time. It does not know which systems you run, how they connect or which rules you follow without ever writing them down. So it guesses, and a confident guess in your accounts is worse than no answer at all.

    Here are five things you can do this month before you let an agent work inside your business. None of them needs a new tool.

    It has been revealed that book two hours with the three or four people who make most of the everyday decisions. Ask them one question: “What would a newly introduced hire ask you in their first week?” The answers are your unwritten rules: which customers get special terms, when a refund is approved, what can be invoiced and what cannot. Write each one as a short sentence, specific enough to check: “This customer gets files back in their own template.” “Refunds above 300 euros are approved by the finance lead.”.

    List every system you use and what each one is the source of truth for. You will find places where two systems describe the same thing differently. “Returned” in the ERP can mean the customer has sent the item back, while in the warehouse it means the item is back on the shelf.

    Recent findings suggest that the instinct is to make the systems agree. In my experience, that rarely works because each system was set up for the team that uses it, and that is why it works for them. Write the translation down instead. The same goes for numbers. In my manufacturer, the price did not sit in the same place from one customer to the next. Note where it lives for whom and which value to trust for which question.

    Most useful answers need two systems joined: the order in the web shop and the invoice in accounting, or the support ticket and the customer in the CRM. Find the field that ties them together and test it by hand. Take 20 random orders and look for them in the other system. If you find 19, you can build on that link. If you find 12, you cannot, and an agent will rarely tell you it is guessing. The test takes an afternoon and saves months of wrong reports.

    Industry observers note that split actions into four levels: read, propose, act after approval and act alone. Start with everything that changes something requiring approval from a named person. Set limits in money and volume, not in trust. When the agent has proposed the same action a hundred times without a mistake, move that one action up a level. That decision should be yours, never the agent’s.

    For every action, record who asked for it, who approved it, what happened and when. It sounds bureaucratic, but it is the only way to answer when a customer, an auditor or your board asks, “Why did this happen?” Without a log, you also cannot tell when it is safe to give the agent more freedom.

    It has been revealed that none of this is about artificial intelligence. It is about making knowledge that lives in people’s heads, and in systems that do not talk to each other, available and trustworthy. Companies that do this get more out of their AI. They also become less fragile when a key person goes on holiday or leaves.

    So start small. Book the two hours this week, write down 10 rules and test one link.

    10 stocks we like better than Salesforce ›.

    Recent findings suggest that salesforce dominates the customer relationship management space, helping businesses track every client interaction. Both companies are now racing to integrate generative AI into their ecosystems, making this a pivotal comparison for investors seeking growth in tech stocks.

    Salesforce provides cloud-based software that connects sales, marketing, and IT on a single platform to serve over 150,000 companies. It has recently prioritized AI integration through a major partnership with Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) for "Copilotforce," which combines customer context with AI experiences. The manufacturer continues expanding its reach through acquisitions such as Braze (BRZE +0.09%) to deepen engagement. The manufacturer also generated net income of roughly $9.7 billion, which reflects a net margin of close to 22%. This growth trend has been supported by a steady increase in revenue from $34.9 billion just two years ago. The business focuses on maintaining profitability while scaling its cloud ecosystem and proprietary AI tools.

    As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.3x, which compares total debt to shareholder equity. The current ratio, a measure of how well a firm covers short-term debts with short-term assets, is approximately 0.8x. In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $14.4 billion. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 23.4% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

    ServiceNow offers an AI platform designed to automate enterprise work across departments including IT, human resources, and finance. The manufacturer focuses on large enterprise clients, ending recent periods with over 600 customers spending more than $5 million annually. It maintains strategic partnerships with Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) and Accenture (ACN +1.19%) to drive AI-driven workflow integrations for its 8,700 total customers. This strategy targets a growing presence in the public sector and large organizations seeking efficient digital transformation.

    It has been revealed that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached close to $15.4 billion, marking revenue growth of approximately 21.8% over the preceding year. ServiceNow reported net income of nearly $1.4 billion for this period, yielding a net margin of approximately 9.4%. While its net margin is lower than its rival, the tech giant has consistently increased its top line from $9.0 billion two years prior. This expansion reflects robust demand for workflow automation tools across global markets.

    As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.2x. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 35.9% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The manufacturer also navigates cybersecurity threats and potential volatility from shifting its pricing models toward consumption-based structures.

    ServiceNow must prove it can continue competing effectively as the AI market evolves rapidly. The company relies on third-party cloud providers and faces regulatory scrutiny related to its growing government contracting business. Additionally, any failure to realize benefits from its aggressive merger and acquisition strategy could impact future growth prospects if integration costs exceed the value gained.
